The campanelle nere with a cheesy yet hot-peppery crab-sauce for 20 dollars were equally disappointing, especially as they rested on a bed of aforementioned cheese (?) sauce (see pictures). I'm not necessarily a purist about mixing fish with cheese, but this just didn't work and the excessive buildup of sauce was frankly off-putting. The best was the glass of Lugana, probably because it definitely didn't come from their kitchen. For two primi and one glass of wine, 64 dollars out the door (including tip, service was fine).

Had a great meal here on a Saturday night - make sure you make reservations because it was packed. We had the following:
-frose drink: this was just ok. I wouldn't order it again but it was fun to try. 
-tomato rice balls: these were amazing, I would definitely recommend 
-prosciutto and buffalo mozzarella: the portion of prosciutto is pretty big and tasted fresh. The mozzarella was good but the portion was small
-stuffed meatballs: these were great and the sauce was amazing
-fiore di carciofi: I didn't love this dish but my husband loved it. It's a small portion so you may want to get an appetizer if you just plan on ordering this
-squid ink pasta: this was our least favorite dish. The crab just made the dish taste very fishy. I wouldn't recommend this.
-branzino: this was my favorite (besides the tomato risotto balls). The sauce was great and the skin was crispy. I would definitely get this again.
Overall, it was a great dinner.
Great  place sal the chef was great delicious appetizers  great lemon  chicken great staff
Place is excellent.  Great pasta dishes and their appetizers (especially the brussel sprouts) were excellent.

Get the Ricotta Crostino, it's one of the best things I've tried! A great balance of sweet and savory from the truffle honey and hazelnuts. I came here when I wasn't too hungry so will return to try more of their dishes. We tried the froses, personally I'm not the biggest frose fan but it was nice to try them out.

Relaxed, cozy vibe with traditional Italian fare. Came here for the frosé, which was a kind of small glass for the price (and considering it's watered down wine), but still yummy. Nice staff. I would come back here again

Went her for dinner and had the antipasti salad, the ricotta bruschetta and the rigatoni carbonara. All were very good and they sat us at a nice table tucked away in the corner. Only complaint was that my carbonara was literally half bacon half pasta as you can tell by my picture. I do love bacon but their pasta is so good I wish I had more of it and less bacon. The pasta was cooked perfectly and was well seasoned. For dessert I had the affagato which was a perfect way to end the meal. Servers were really nice and service was quick but you didn't feel rushed which was nice.

Our server was in a rush from the second we sat down. She asked us 3 times to order within 15 minutes of sitting. Once we decided, we ordered 3 appetizers to share. We noticed that the table next to us received bread but we were not served that which is weird considering we got meatballs. The food arrived within 6 minutes of ordering and everything was piping hot. Once we finished (less than 20 minutes) our server came over another 2 times within 10 minutes to get us to order more. We finally decided to share a spaghetti dish as we already had 3 apps + drinks and the dishes looked big. When we ordered the dish our server said "really? That's it?" We said yes. She was noticeably pissed. Again the food came within 5 minutes. Overall between being rushed by our server + bus boy + the food coming overwhelmingly fast, we left within 50 minutes. What was supposed to be a girls night out turned into a $150 50 minute experience.

We came here with reservations and was seated after a few minutes. 

We started with the frose's. It was good but given the price point, it would have been to have the glass filled at least half way. We ordered stuffed meatballs and burrata cremosa. They were both very good especially the stuffed meatballs, the burrata was good, it had a little too much pepper in my opinion. As for the entrees we ordered the linguine, orecchiette, and the fiore di carciofi. All three pasta dishes were fantastic however the portion size is smaller than other Italian restaurants near by. We ordered extra focaccia and bread with olive oil, the bread was dry and hard but ok after dipping it into the left over sauces in the pasta dishes. We ended with the tiramisu, it was ok way too strong for me and its my go to dessert everywhere. Overall the experience was great, the server could have been more friendly but she was busy so we'll let that go.

I should preface this by saying the place is cute and the service is pretty good. However I was looking specifically for frose in the area, and it was the worst frose I've ever tasted. It tasted like a mix of frozen red and white boxed wine. I went with 3 people and none of us could finish and we are by no means wine snobs. When we clearly weren't drinking the frose at the bar they didn't check in and let us tab out with nearly full glasses. I'm assuming they know their product is bad.

Great friendly service and the bensonhurst sandwich was really good.  We were in a situation with our airbnb on 5/24 and the staff was accommodating with our luggage and gave us a delicious tira misu dessert on the house. Made a disappointing day a little better. Thank you!

I like Italian food, but I can also make pasta dishes at home that are decent enough, so often pass over pasta restaurants. Then I go to a place like Bar Primi and realize my mistake.

It's all about the pasta here. It's probably a very American thing to go to an Italian restaurant and not even look at the secondi options like chicken and steak. So here, there are no pretenses. The two of us got the pesto penne, sausage and broccoli rabe orecchiete, and squid ink campanelle. All so good they made me kick myself for not going out to eat more pasta. 

Will have to be back soon to try out the rest of their pastas!

Love going here for a quick lunch with a friend or a late dinner. The frozen rosés are great and the pasta is flavorful. The atmosphere is very chic and located directly in soho right near all the great stores. The prices aren't bad especially for the portion sizes. However, it does get extremely busy on weekends so I'd highly recommend making a reservation prior to dining.

I found Bar Primi on a list of best NYC brunch places that take reservations. It was easy to make and modify my reservation on Open Table. The servers were kind and attentive, but let us take our time with our meal. The atmosphere was bright and open, but cozy. It was busy, but not packed so our group had plenty of room to spread out.
We all ordered our own entrees including the almond granola, funghi scramble, breakfast spaghetti, and penne. Each entree was enough food for one hungry person. While I'm typically a breakfast person at brunch, the pastas were the winners here. The breakfast spaghetti had the breakfast tastes of pancetta and egg on top of a delicious pasta. The penne was just a really well done pasta! I think that would be my dish of choice if I were to return.
Overall, Bar Primi is a great place for a brunch reservation, but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat there.

Headed there for dinner with friends. 
As a coeliac I asked for the Gf version on the squid ink. 
Turned out to be really great, the service was fast. Was a bit afraid to have a bland taste but it was really well seasoned and the texture of the pasta was flawless
If you prefer a more quiet spot ask to be seated upstairs.

Would have given them more STARS  except for the cool aloof reception upon arrival. AND the fact they we were here to celebrate an important "30"
BD dinner before an evening of spoken word at The Bowery Poetry Club down the street. They made our Birthday Boy who is an amputee and was obvious because he was shorts climb the stairs for a table of three
and YES we did have a reservation 
No thought No compassion No accommodation 
OFF to a good start 
Then we met Frank  our waiter quiet reserved yet charming informed and helpful  We also had Colin explaining dishes and helping with gluten free pasta options which are abundant except for the stuffed pasta 
Appetizers we shared three - yummy ricotta crostini, delish rice balls- and fabulous roasted Brussels  sprouts 
All good and easy to share 
We ordered separate pasta dishes - the spaghetti  pomodoro - the bucatini lamb amatriciana and rigatoni carbonara - all fabulous, tasty and cooked perfectly. 
Aside from good food when they learn to be mindful of the special needs of their paying customers especially the ones that are really looking for a Bowery restaurant to accommodate dinners before the Poetry shows 
Having special needs - we have to fight enough - we shouldn't have to fight for a table on the ground floor OPEN YOUR EYES and YOUR MIND and YOUR HEART and THINK how would YOU would like to be treated and then adjust your attitude  and otherwise the food is good

Dined here this evening.  
Food was delicious, and service was outstanding.  Manager could not be more attentive! Highly recommend the rice balls, branzino, and the bucatini.

Nice ambience, however the service left a lot to be desired unfortunately. The servers were nice and polite, but it seemed to be disorganized and slow. They were on point when it came to filling our water glasses, but our "main" server went around to filling all the other table's water before taking our order.

The pasta dishes were good but nothing extraordinary. The squid ink pasta was the standout.

Overall the lackluster service was detrimental to our overall experience, especially since it was our friend's bday we were celebrating.

Would cautiously recommend if you are a pasta lover and they up their service and waiting game.

Yahhsss Bar Primi. I'm convinced the only and best way to come here is to do the pre fix family style dinner with a group of 8-10. You will need a reservation, and can grab a drink at the bar beforehand. 

The food and service is outstanding. We had waiters surrounding our table the entire time checking on us. Memorable dishes included grilled octopus, this amazing ricotta bread, nearly raw steak and the passssstaaaa.  

I'm coming back ASAP.
One of the best Italian resturaunt that hits the spot! Dishes are amazing full with flavors. Deff a romantic place for dinner date, birthday dinner.

Came here with a group of four and I thought that the food was just okay. The pastas are mostly around $17-25, which is pretty pricey compared to some other places I've been to in NYC. The ambiance in the restaurant is really nice and is great for dates or a nice dinner with friends. I personally was not a huge fan of the food though. 

I ordered the linguini (~$17), which was basically just a garlic pasta with breadcrumbs. For what it was, I thought that it was a little overpriced and tasted very average. There was just a lot of butter/oil at the bottom of my dish and I got bored with the dish mid way, which never happens when I eat pasta!!! The portions also weren't very large. 

Overall, pretty average experience. I don't think I would want to return--I'd rather spend my money elsewhere for a more memorable meal.
Amazing place! Good service and Excellent food. My boyfriend love it too. The decoration is so nice you must go second floor is so romantic!

Some of the best pasta I've had in a long time! Came here with a group of six for a friend's birthday. The staff was very attentive and accommodating. We ordered the following to share: calamari, spinach fusilli, squid ink campanelle, linguine, and bucatini. I highly recommend the spinach fusilli and squid ink - those were heavenly. The tiramisu here was also delicious, and they put a candle in it for the birthday girl. I can't wait to be back.
Food is amazing!! So affordable. Small portions and long waits but well worth it! Repeat customer

Easy Description:
HORRIBLE SERVICE. Great food, Great atmosphere. 
....Maybe next return we'll sit at the bar and eat, because wait staff is terrible.

This place was... fine. Overall thought it was way too overpriced for the quality of food. Think this is just another trendy establishment but overall nothing that excited me or stood out to me (other than the absurdly high prices). Four of us came with a reservation on a weeknight and were able to be seated right away though the service was a little slow throughout the night. 

We ordered the burrata and stuffed meatballs as apps, and all of us got a different pasta: spinach fusilli, orecchiette, fiore di carciofi, and the squid ink campanelle. The squid ink for sure stole the night - it was delightful and just the right amount of salty. I thought the burrata was a little small and way too covered in peppers. The stuffed meatballs were pretty good too, though nothing about it stood out to me. I didn't love the spinach fusilli or the orecchiette -- again, theme of the night seems to be "it was fine" so they weren't bad dishes but again probably not worth the high price tag for a normal pasta dish. I didn't try the fiore di cariofi because I'm not a huge fan of artichoke but my friends enjoyed it though they said it also seemed too small of a portion.  

My friends were actually still pretty hungry after and we decided to get ice cream somewhere else, but that was pretty telling to me considering how much our total bill came out to be. Don't think this place is worth the money when there's so much other great Italian in the city.

This is my third time coming to this Bar Primi, and it didn't disappoint. The atmosphere was great, and the service was wonderful. I would highly recommend the squink ink campanelle. It's my go-to​ every time!

Suggestion: Make a reservation! The weekends can get busy!

Had to sign up for yelp just to write this review -- was excited to eat at this place with some friends on a quiet wednesday summer night in late august.  arrived at 5:50 and noticed 10 -15 empty tables outside -- wasnt a soul around at that time. literally nobody! hostess insisted she wouldnt seat us until all of us were here and that we should start a tab at the bar.. after repeatedly asking her is she understood how ridiculous that was and she repeatedly insisting we do it her way-- decided to eat next door at gemma.. note to management -- dont hire robots who enforce later in the night policies when the restaurant is full when your restaurant is empty! we went next door to gemma and paid over $400 dollars for drinks and dinner....when you go out of business and wonder what went wrong. .you can re-read this post....morons..  ill give one star bc i have to give something but really a 0

this place was easy to get a reservation at on a thursday night just because the place is big. there's outdoor seating and 2 levels of indoor seating based on what you're going for. read a lot of reviews about bad service but our waiter was lovely and i never had a half-empty water glass. the food was very good and the portion sizes didn't make me feel uncomfortably full. will definitely be back!
It was just ok. Coming back from vacation in Italy food had no taste at Primi. Not memorable, slow service.

I really enjoy this place! The rice balls are amazing! The pesto that comes on top of them is creamy and delicious! The garlic linguine is so yummy( but dangerously garlic-y so beware!) the burrata appetizer is so creamy and the roasted peppers and foccia that comes with it are also amazing! Such great ambience. The restaurant is so cozy and inviting. A place I can spend hours at just eating and socializing with friends! Can't wait to go back!

Very good ambience. Good flavors. Good portion size. 
Had the linguini and the spaghetti pomodoro. The pomodoro delicious. Linguini was bathed in olive oil. Would have preferred if it was made with lesser oil but still delicious.

Best thing about this was getting seated and served quickly. We had gone to a gallery opening two doors over and had 40 mins to eat and dash, and this trendy stalwart did not disappoint. It did however fall short in delivering something memorable for the hefty price tag. The Brussels sprouts were done well - perfectly charred and softened w just enough olive oil - but the rigatoni was very ordinary and carried an overload of cheese and cream. In general, did not live up to the hype.

I've gone to Bar Primi twice now and both times the food and service have been excellent. The kale salad, burrata and stuffed meatballs are a great way to start your meal. Recommended dishes (the pasta is so fresh):
Penne Bolognese
Bucatini with lamb
Orecchiette with broccoli rabe
Ricotta agnolotti

We also had a bottle of Nebbiolo and finished the meal off with their amazing tiramisu and home made gelato. 

Whenever i go back I want to try the branzino because it looked fantastic. Such a great spot in a fun neighborhood with plenty of options to go out afterward.

Probably one of the biggest disappointments and rip offs I've purchased on grub hub. The picture I attached is YOUR version of lamb bucatini amatriciana. First, there was NO lamb in that ragu sauce; only flakes here and there (notice this sauce looks like a pomodoro than a hearty lamb ragu) Secondly, you overcooked the pasta which in Bucatini is terrible as the noodles get slimy and because they are large hollow noodles, the texture is nauseating. For $30 I'm sort of appalled that you don't take pride in your dish and execute a $30 pasta and do it well. This is exactly why I am devoted to places like Lupa and don't eat pasta anywhere else.

Bar Primi deserves 5 stars!!! I'm surprised of the rating but I had nothing but great experience here. Went here with some friends for dinner and we just sat at the bar. LOVED the ambiance and service/food was amazing. Pasta are pretty much are homemade and fresh. I'd definitely come back again! 

Things I ordered/must get: 
- ricotta crostino hazelnuts, truffle honey 
- beets pistachio pesto, pimenton yogurt
- cauliflower cacio e pepe, tutto spic
- spaghetti pomodoro parmigiano-reggiano
- squid ink campanelle crab, garlic crema, fresno

Come for happy hour, stay for the good food. I came here with a couple of coworkers and had a great time. They have a terrific happy hour drink and food menu which I highly recommend. In the summer they are also quite popular for their frose. Everything was delicious and I would happily come back again.

The food here was good, typical NYC brunch items and prices. The service was not equal to the food, we were served after three tables that were seated after us, one table near us had to have the order corrected three times. I will not go back.

Went here on a Sunday night with a group to celebrate a special birthday and had a very unpleasant and unnecessarily long dining experience. It was a larger group (10) which I guess was confusing because our wait staff messed everything we ordered up repeatedly. It took them 4 trips to the table to get the correct food on the table because they sent all the wrong dishes and the runners didn't know what they had in their hands. Then because we were repeatedly sent the wrong food our bill had to be redone several times as well. We had a vegan and someone with a dairy allergy at the table and both of them had entrees with cheese placed in front of them multiple times. One of my vegetarian friends was assured she received the correct entree but it ended up having meat in it. I do feel slightly bad giving this place a bad review because the food is amazing and at the end the main woman serving us was trying her best but the experiences soured what should've been a very celebratory meal and made it a 3+ hour long affair on a Sunday night when we all had work the next day. We were comped two appetizers but that didn't really make up for the troubles.

This was recommended to us. Great atmosphere, limited variety menu. Service was one of the worst we have ever experienced. Support staff was great but the waiter made us feel as if we were putting him out. He did not introduce himself, was not helpful with menu choices, never checked to see how we were doing. The restaurant opened at 5:30 & we had a 5:45 reservation. The pumpkin ravioli was barely warm, my meal was quite good and fine for a small appetite, rice balls were terribly bland. We would not consider this venue for dinner again.

I have to say - I think this place may be overhyped. It always come up in conversation as a top, rustic Italian restaurant but I don't know if I see it that way.

I went in on a Thursday night with a reservation - it took 20 minutes past my reservation time to seat me. For an italian restaurant, they don't even give out bread baskets? Ok...nevermind, we order rice balls. The rice balls were probably my favorite part of the meal. Fried to perfection, crisp, and served with yummy sauce - all a win.

Next up, my friend and I chose to split two pastas - spaghetti carbonara & lamb ragu. This is where I started to question the meal. The carbonara was OK but really just typical, nothing too special about it. The lamb ragu was good but the lamb was worked into the sauce, there weren't even chunks of lamb!

3 stars for ambiance, good wine, and good rice balls. I just don't know if it's worth returning.

Fun place! It was super busy when my friend and I decided to stop by on a Wednesday night, but we had a reservation and were able to be seated pretty quickly. Seemed to be more of a young crowd there, and there were a lot of people hanging out at the bar. The lights are dim, and the atmosphere was chill. My friend and I ordered two frosés to start and ordered two different pasta dishes. They brought bread out, which was good. I, personally, wasn't a big fan of the frosé, so I ordered a different drink for after dinner. Overall, great place, great vibes, and good food. I'd definitely stop in again!

I got it, y'all are in NYC BUT why ya gotta do us dirty with that pricing tho? Also side note, service is pretty damn slow even when the restaurant is empty. 

I dined in for brunch with my friends when they first opened & y'all it's not perfect for pretty brunch pictures bc that lighting is DIM. 

I tried the highly yelp recommended breakfast pasta. I don't know about y'all but how do you guys eat a $21.75 pasta and think that's OK? Y'all are bougie up in here. 

While I agree the kale, pancetta, poached egg and pasta had a great flavor balance it just wasn't worth the deep price. Is it filling? HELL yeah!
And for you kale haters, it's actually pretty good in here. It adds that vegetable balance to this super decadent bowl of cream, cheese and fat. 

So would I recommend? Of course if that Tinder date or SD is taking you so y'all don't gotta pay.

Staff were super friendly, food was really good, great atmosphere. I took my gf here for her bday and we both loved it. I told the staff in advance and they added a few nice touches like wishing happy bday and bringing candles on the desert.

Had my first night's dinner here on a business trip a couple weeks ago.

It's date-night dark inside and very cozy.  My friend and I sat almost elbow-to-elbow to the couple next to us that actually were on a date.

For starters we shared the stuffed meatballs in sugo...very delicious.  They were some healthy, ping pong sized balls.  For my entree I had the penne ragu alla bolognese, ricotta.  The ricotta is a really nice touch as I don't usually get things with it.  Dessert was all about the almond gelati.  I try to steer clear of almond flavored stuff cuz usually things just end up tasting like fake almond extract but that was not the case here and lapped it all up.

Prosecco was my drink of choice, nothing exceptional.

I liked this place for many reasons.  It was walking distance from my hotel.  I liked the low-key ambiance, my meal was great, and the service was prompt and friendly.  

Definitely worth a come back.

Came here for a birthday dinner with two of my girlfriends and we were IN LOVE! They have a great selection of wine and the servers were extremely helpful when trying to select what entrees to order. 
The three of us shared the Risotto Arencini as appetizer which I HIGHLY recommend! We then got 2 pasta dishes as an entree to share. The pasta was cooked so well and it ended up being more than enough food for the three of us. Loved this place!

A perfect place to eat if you're not hungry...

On the positive side, Bar Primi combines warm ambiance, attentive staff and tasty food (we started the meal with the rice balls which were delicious and we were definitely enthused). 
However, the portions are prohibitively small. The lamb amatriciana pasta was just about OK (though by no means filling) - but the fiori di carciofi was just ridiculously tiny. So tiny in fact, that the dish consisted of only one single (admittedly long) pasta. Yes, you read that right: ONE SINGLE PASTA.  The icing on the cake was that they have the guts to charge $20+ for this dish. We left the restaurant hungry and hugely unsatisfied. 
Obviously we won't be going back.
Great pastas, apps could be better. Squid ink, lamb and garlic pastas were flavorful. Great selection of wine and quick service.

Great cuisine and excellent service. So many choices on the menu popped out to to me but I started with the rice balls. They were amazing and came with some sort of pesto cream sauce. Choosing an entree was a challenge between the cacio e pepe, steak sandwich and the squid ink pasta with crab meat. I went with the crab pasta and it has the perfect amount of peppers/spice. Wine list was very Italian in varietal. Service was attentive and my water glass was always full. Ambiance was dark and intimate, would recommend if you're in the area and in the mood for Italian.

We had a very decent meal here - it was super busy yet service was pretty good. Food was good, decent wine list, overall we found it a really good time, without feeling like we were getting ripped off.

The pasta was amazing esp the squid ink pasta  and the carbonara pasta... but besides that the whole atmosphere is great.. i will say this the waiter i had was no help idk if it was me but i felt like he felt a certain way because of my date FYI she was a beautiful light skinned female.. i notice he was much nicer with the group of girls next to our table and when i asked about which pasta was good because FYI I'm not Italian lol he gave a vague respond and even when i asked him what was a good recommendation for beer he gave me another vague answer but other then that the food is amazing but that waiter ruined the vibe for me and my date

This place has really gone downhill. They constantly change their menu. My girlfriend ordered delivery here and after an hour she called this place about the food. They said that they had a problem with the system and the food would be on the way with free desert. She later received a call from grub hub saying the order was canceled and the restaurant closed for the night. It was very unprofessional and a trash move.

I have to knock off a star but its because of the website or the restaurant week lunch menu. 

I walk into a beautiful and rustic space. I love Locanda Verde and I know chef Andrew Carmellini will create a most casual restaurant with amazing pasta. I see on the restaurant week menu an offering for paccheri with white veal bolognese and piava. Heck, I don't know what piava is but I'm down if its from Chef Carmellini.

I see the restaurant week lunch special has spaghetti with white veal bolognese?? (Don't forget the piava) Not a problem, I want to try the white veal bolognese, something different. 

The wine is substantial, I ordered a nice Italian red wine to get the dining started. I ordered the calamari fritti with spicy peppers. The peppers were amazing. The calamari was good, it wasn't tough but the coating looked dark. I still knocked it out.

My pasta comes to me and man does it look good. My first bite? Creamy and dreamy. White veal bolognese, I'm tasting a lot of cream sauce, the freshly made pasta makes this dish wonderful. Where's the piava?! I wanted to ask for red pepper flakes but I didn't want to create a faux pas my first time dining here. 

I would have loved to try the paccheri with regular red bolognese. I think my wife would flip over this place, hopefully I'll return soon.

To be continued
Not sure how meatballs stuffed with cheese and bathed in sauce are dry, but they somehow were. Bready, no real flavor other than salt, just disappointing. The ricotta toast was decent though.

We went during 2/2019 restaurant week. Food was beyond excellent. We usually go to many Italian restaurant and we don't often want to go back to any. But this was one of those we would go back. The chicken Marsala mushroom was one of the best I've ever had. The paccheri white veal bolognese was also so tasty. The service was fast-- we were able to get food and eat within 45 minutes to catch our show. Malcolm was our waiter and he did wonderful. Happy hour is from 3:30pm to 6:30pm daily from Monday to Friday. They thought it ended at 5:30pm so we had to remind them. Otherwise the service and food was top top notch

It was ok overall. The food was nice but nothing special frankly. The service was not great. First they were very slow, took them awhile to take orders. Then they started rushing, taking away plates while we were still eating. Ambiance was ok, the restaurant felt a little crowded

Atmosphere is nice, food is middle-of-the-road. Came with a group of 6 on a Sunday for brunch (you can make reservations, which is nice). We had:

-Ricotta Crostino: tasty, heavy on the truffle 
-Burrata Cremosa: probably my favorite; the foccacia bread was the best part 
-Italian Benedict: this is where things went a bit south. The poached eggs were completely cooked through (which should never happen)...the sauce was a really simple tomato sauce and the meat was thick. The flavor was a bit too one-dimensional for me...

I would come back to try the breakfast spaghetti - that looked good!

Three stars because my friends, family and I used to love this place. We came here all the time and the staff was very friendly and hospitable. The food was also great. Recently, I've been disappointed by the food and the service. The last time I went to the location, the waitress walked into me three times while I was sitting. I ordered something online, waited for an hour and a half, called and spoke to someone that my food was on the way, only to shortly then be called by the third party delivery service that they canceled the order...

Went here on a Friday with an early reservation at 6:30. The service was friendly and fast. The inside was very cute, rustic with hanging lights. The seating was intimate, I'm glad I was not on a first day since we were sitting in a corner table basically on top of each other in the upstairs section. Highly recommend you start with the burrata and the stuffed meatballs, the portions are small so we were glad we ordered two items for two people to share. 

The focaccia bread that came with burrata was amazing! I asked for more focaccia to soak up the remainder of the burrata and peppers and the waiter gladly and quickly brought me some more about two minutes after I asked. 

My boyfriend loved the Italian Old Fashioned cocktail. We both cleaned our entree pasta dishes - I don't think you can go wrong with any pasta dish. The portion looked small, but I walked out of their incredibly full. The pasta was al dente and not overly salty. Unfortunately we were too full to order dessert. I would definitely recommend friends to go here!

Great ambiance, great food, great service. The meatballs, the Penne and the Bucatini were all delicious. Our waiter recommended an amazing (and affordable!) bottle of wine. Will definitely be coming back here!

I knew I wanted squid ink pasta and that NYC would be the perfect place to find it.  I sought out a place that was near Union Square, open late, and had a decently-priced menu.  I walked in on Sunday night expecting not much of a crowd, but this placed was packed to the gills.  I opted for bar seating, and asked for a wine recommendation with my cauliflower appetizer and squid ink Campanelle crab pasta.  The white wine (unsure of the varietal) was a great pick by the bartender.  The cauliflower and pasta both had cream sauces, which was a miss on my end--I should have opted for a lighter app or pasta.  I was also surprised to see a squid ink pasta dressed w/cream sauce, but I figured I would try something new.  The cauliflower was cacio pepe style with the perfect amount of onion, and the squid ink pasta was perfectly al dente.  Great texture, though they could have been a little more generous on the crab meat.  What made the pasta for me though was the slivers of habanero pepper, which added a subtle bite to an otherwise understated dish.  Despite the heaviness of the dishes, I absolutely loved the vibe of Bar Primi.  It was diverse, full of couples, single people, wingmen looking out for each other, and single women reveling in their single lady-hood.  The scene is great w/o being pretentious, and I'd be confident returning by myself to enjoy a glass of wine on a very busy night.  Stars for being open late.
Wayyyyy overpriced for what you're getting. 16$ glass of wine and stale bread (if you ask for it). Pasta is delicious so stick to that!
Excellent pasta dishes with a deep wine menu! Restaurant is quite beautiful and has great energy!

We were trying to find a place to grab dinner on a Friday night and lucky for us Bar Primi was available! It did get pretty crowded around 8PM though, so you might just get lucky earlier in the night.

We shared a $45 bottle of wine and $11 rice balls. I ordered the $26 squid ink campanelle crab for my entree and the $12 tiramisu for dessert. The quality of food and the ambiance would make this a four star experience; but the quantity of food and prices bump it down for me to three stars.

The food here was delicious. We had a larger group so we got the family-style chef's choice. The food was incredible. Everyone at the table loved the bolognese and many people were saying that the Brussels sprout appetizer was the best Brussels sprouts they had ever had. The wait staff was incredibly attentive and friendly. Would absolutely do this for a large group again!

A solid 3 stars. 

This restaurant had great service, ample seating, and mood lighting. However, it's like the safety restaurant of the area: this is where you go when the other restaurants are busy. 

The food is tasty, but the price doesn't match the value. The portions are small and the dishes are very basic Italian pasta and 3 entree options. No salads available. The portions are small, but that ended up being a good thing because I felt just the right level of fullness after! 

It's an okay place and I'm glad I tried it!
Love the pasta here and the frozé. The food is presented beautifully and the staff are completely genuine. In the summer, it's fun to sit outside and sip on some drinks.

Went to this place with my sister and friend. The food was good but expensive with somewhat small portions for how much they cost. We started with the meatballs appetizer - those were excellent. They have an excellent red sauce recipe. I got the house-made pasta special for my entree- it was just okay.  Their pesto sauce was  bland and over compensated by Parmesan cheese, however the house made pasta had a perfect texture so it saved the dish. I might go back and give other dishes a taste.

I came here for the  first time in a while.
I already knew here is nice interior decor and tasty and good service.

Therefore I brought my client for dinner  at 6:30 PM
It was quiet and less people ( absolutely comfy)

Nobody bring menu nor attention for a while
( maybe it just opened and bit hectic ?)

Meanwhile, a guy looks like a manager brought  menu and explained  special menu of the day 
" Veal bolognese  white sauce pasta " 

1 st waiter came to take an order
And he suggested  sone veggies and meat, also he gave us some idea to order. 
Then we order Brussels sprout and Meat ball as starter. Both was really good!

We were still thinking about main meal and see how much room left with our stomach ..
So we decided one pasta for share. 

2nd waiter come ( different from 1 st waiter) 
Finally took out order "today's special pasta" $24

When the pasta  came , it looked  bit meat sauce ( not white sauce) but  lots of cheese on it, I wasn't sure yet.

After while , we realized it was  totally different from the special menu that we were explained..

I try to ask them but I couldn't do that since my client already started eating and I didn't want to get in trouble and her to be worried.  

I was wondering if I misunderstood his explanation of the menu,  but the special pasta  would be same as $24. Or so. 

After all, we figure out The pasta was " lobster tomato sauce $33 on the bill 
Huge difference  from " veal white sauce $24 

I claimed  the guy ( manager ?) who explain today's special to wrong order, even though  we completely finished eating . 
But , We thought today's special was  $24  but they charge us $33 for it! That doesn't make sense to me. 

Besides  the waiter who took our order didn't know exactly Today's special, neither confirmed with us.
I guess he just brought most expensive pasta aka "special pasta" 

The manager apologized us the confusion and could weave $10 from the bill. 

I meant this is not a complain at all  more like  applause their service and hospitality and thoughtfulness.

Okay this is my second time here and it is Michelin rated on Bib Gourmand as well as a lot of great reviews word of mouth. The atmosphere and service is great, very cozy with lots of candles. I got the special cacio e Pepe with kale and it was pretty bland, not as creamy as I expected as well as the kale was very salty. I just can't justify the price for the amount and quality of food. It's a fun time and nice to hang out there with a drink but pretty pricy for what you get

For all your frozè lovers I think bar primi is the home of froze- I LOVE froze and the best one I ever had has to be from here. I'd never think to pair froze with pasta but I have to tell you it is the best decision I ever made and you will enjoy the pairing!

One of the worst dining experiences in recent memory! Arrived at 6:50p for a table of 2 - the place was mostly empty and we were seated quickly upstairs. After waiting 15 minutes, we finally got water. Another 30 minutes, and the waitress (Tricia) finally got our order. I saw that the other tables were being serviced regularly and immediately. A couple that sat down maybe 20 minutes after we had arrived had already received their appetizers and placed their order. We got our appetizer and realized we were the only table that didn't get bread for the table. I had to flag down several servers to ask for bread. Almost an hour into the dining experience and we had no one asking or checking on us. Finally at 7:50pm I flagged down the waitress (who was visibly ignoring us), and asked her where our main courses were as we had been waiting for an hour. She remarked that she was waiting for us to finish our appetizers before bringing our food !!??? I said we've been done for awhile. She never stopped by and asked if we were working on it etc. After another 30 min, we finally got our main courses. The food was mediocre at best and not worth the hassle of the night. We quickly got our bill and left immediately - food unfinished. A terrible experience for what we were hoping would be a nice weeknight date. Will never go back!

If I could give this 3.75, I prob would...but it's def. closer to 4 than 3. The ambiance was chic and cool and the food was very solid; not amazing, but good. No regrets. 

My favorite part of the night was actually the "money" hazy IPA, it was really good (If you are into north eastern style IPA's). 

Ricotta crustini - 4 out of 5
Cauliflower caccio pepe- 3 out of 5
Carbonara- 4 out of 5 
Tirimisu- 4 out of 5

Overall, I would recommend trying it out, i'll be back.

Decent place to check out. Vibe is nice, came here on a Wednesday evening and we shared the large communal table in the front since we didn't have reservations. Tried the frose, which was okay. Prices are definitely on the higher end and the portions are small as others have mentioned. Also they don't give out bread and olive oil which I find to be weird. Haven't been to an Italian restaurant especially for dinner where they don't give bread.

Surprised by how lively this place was on a Wednesday night & how good the food was. My lovely mother & I split an arugula salad, spicy shrimp pasta, & steak entree (and obviously a couple bottles of wine). The wine was good, the salad was tasty, the shrimp pasta simple but satisfying & a very very good steak. I recommend this sharing some dishes to get a taste of the menu. Perfect place for a date. We ended the night with the almond gelato, perfect ending.

Would give this zero stars if I could. we made a reservation here specifically to sit outside (and put this in our reservation) after being told repeatedly it wouldn't be possible (without much explanation either - the patio was empty) we finally agreed to sit inside. I went downstairs minutes later and they had filled up the patio with everyone filing up the spots and they told us there was no room. Horribly run, mistake to come here, food subpar drinks bad and WORST SERVICE I've ever received in New York. Just rude.

They open the terrace for us during a sunny afternoon.
Sorry to trouble your organisation but thank you for the perfect family lunch during our vacation.
The absolute worst service. Was seated 45 minutes late and was not comped for any of the meal... was given a glass of Prosecco and that's all. Horrible management. Would not recommend.

Came here for lunch per a recommendation of a friend.

The lunch specials are pretty solid! I ordered the linguine with garlic and breadcrumbs. I enjoy really simple pastas, so if that's your kinda thing - I recommend it!

My boyfriend ordered the squid ink campanelle. He enjoyed his, but it was a little too creamy for me. Again, depends on your palette. If you like creamy pastas, that might the one for you. :) 

I do think there are other spots that are probably tastier, but for the lunch special offerings, I give this 4 stars.

Good service, delicious food, nice size portions, nice wine list.....
Have the chianti

The atmosphere was fun and decorous.  The waitstaff were very good.  On Saturday night I ordered the special, veal and green salad.  The salad was superb.  Very fresh greens and tomatoes.  The veal, however, was quite poor.  It was a thin breaded cutlet that was very overcooked and the flavor was basically of breaded oil.  It was so dry that I asked for a side of red sauce which did help matters.  The rest of my party did better but my dish was lacking,especially considering it was the night's special.

Best pancakes in NYC. Delicious brunch! Bright room for brunch which is nice. Good for birthday brunch or any other occasion as well! If you sit outside be sure to wear sun protection! I still have a terrible tan line weeks later
The branzino tiramisu and pasta were all fresh tasting. Chic city vibe ambiance. Wish they gave bread and oil while we waited for the food though!

Came here for brunch on Saturday and the food was terrible. They got the order wrong twice and when the food actually came it inedible. The eggs were extremely undercooked and the meal was flavorless.  No-one even asked how the meal was when it was collected even though it was hardly touched.

Stopped by 10:30/11pm on Cinco de mayo night (Sunday). Even though we were the 2nd to last table of the night, our waiter and server were attentive and fantastic. Nice and comfortable setting. Thanks for a great experience.

This is one of my FAV restaurants in Bowery, it is right by Broadway so its perfect to eat here before shopping in SOHO. I highly recommend the squid ink pasta with crab meat, and spicy chilis - AMAZING. I also highly recommend the burrata or the ricotta with honey on a crostini 10/10. The frose is also one of my personal favorites and if you are a frose fan, you must try theirs! The service is always great, the food is always amazing and the location is ideal!

Outstanding! I am so glad I finally made it here. I've had it on my list forever. This place was amazing and I loved it. We ordered the squid ink pasta with crab which is so flavorful and delicious. Sometimes the crab flavor can be lost, but not here! Delicious! We also ordered the burrata which is amplified by the red peppers but you only need one per cheese bite otherwise the peppers take over the flavor. 

We also ordered the carbonara pasta but neither of us like cabbage, so the waiter recommended kale instead. The kale was cooked which complimented the dish nicely and was delicious with the thick cut bacon and cream sauce. We finished with a cappuccino. I can't wait to come back!

This is by far a great date night restaurant. I had the "frosse" cocktail which was delicious but small in size. My boyfriend & I shared the squid ink crab meat pasta and the spaghetti & clams which were both very delicious.  I definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone who enjoys Italian food.

Stopped by on a nice spring afternoon today, and sat outside. Service is fast and extremely patient. Ordered the pesto pasta with asparagus. Very simple dish, yet the portion was so small! Was this for a baby hamster??! I was left unsatisfied and hungry after. Sadly this place has decent food but it's burning a hole in your pockets. Would not pay this much again as there are other Italian options in the area since it's off Little Italy.

I LOVED this place. I went on their 5th Birthday and sat at the bar. David has been there almost since they opened and gives the best recommendations. We started with frose that originated there! It was deceivingly strong and not sweet, which it's not supposed to be! We tried the rigatoni carbonara which is a must with thick cut pieces of bacon. We also tried the bucatini cacio e pepe which was cooked perfectly al debate. We also had the Nutella Sundae, which they make everything except the Nutella sauce in house. Bottom line, it's usually pretty expensive, but portions are big so come with friends and try things!

Went here with 3 friends for their 5 year anniversary and $5 pasta dishes. Needless to say, we ordered 8 of their 10 pasta dishes to share as a group.

Overall, I have to say that this place is probably more of a 3.5 star level as I would say I was a big fan of about 4 of the pastas, 3 of them were good, and 1 of them was just ok. The paccheri and the bucatini were my two favorites and my least favorite was actually the squid ink pasta.

The service itself was limited--and maybe because it was $5 pasta night--but our table outside was splendid on a beautiful night.

Solid place for pastas, but my favorite was the appetizers. We shared everything family style so I was able to get a taste of everything.

Appetizers:
* Ricotta crostino, hazelnuts, truffle honey - This was my favorite appetizer. It sounds simple, but it was really good to start the meal with. I'm happy they put so many chopped hazelnuts on top.
* Cauliflower cacio e pepe - The cauliflower was so cheesy, it basically wasn't a vegetable anymore. Take two lactaids if you are lactose intolerant. Looks like they have an asparagus version of this now.
* Tutto spice stuffed meatballs in sugo - I liked the other two appetizers better, but there were also good to order.

Pastas:
* Ricotta agnolotti, vodka sugo, prosciutto - This was one of my favorites because I love stuffed pastas in general and the filling was soft. The little pieces of prosciutto tasted like sausage.
* Squid ink campanelle crab, garlic crema, fresno - This was also one of my favorites. The sauce is slightly spicy and very creamy. Gimme more crab please!!
* Spaghetti & clams 'nduja sausage sugo, parsley - Another person in my group liked this one. I mostly enjoyed the texture of the breadcrumbs they put on top.
* Fiore di carciofi pancetta, pecorino - This was one literally one long noodle. You can't go wrong with pancetta and pecorino, but not sure I'd order this again.

It was easy to get a reservation here, so this might be a good place for last minute dinner plans.

I had been wanting to try this place for forever and finally got a chance. We made reservations a week out for 8pm. We ordered the stuffed meatballs and the ricotta crostini to start. The meatballs were good but the ricotta crostini was amazing! Probably the best ricotta I have ever had. For mains, we got the linguine, penne and agnolotti (agnolotti not pictured because they gave us the wrong dish initially). The penne was delicious with another dallop of that unreal ricotta. The agnolotti was also seriously yummy. While still good, the linguine wasn't anything special compared to the other two. The service was pretty good and I am definitely excited to come back soon!

They told us the wait for a table outside would be around 30minutes. We put our name and number down. Walked around and came back to wait at the bar. 45 mins later we ask the hostess when we can expect to be seated, she says there are still a number of people ahead of us, so another half hour, not apologetic or sympathetic. Ok fine. 1.5 hours after I put my name down, my friend attempts to find out what's going on. She gets another emotionless response. Finally we get seated. Almost 2 hours later. If we had known the wait would be that long, we would have gone somewhere else. Not worth the wait.

Went to Bar Primi a few weeks ago to celebrate their 5th birthday with $5 pastas! Everything f was delicious! We got the Bucatini, the penne pasta, and the squid ink campanelle. All of the pastas has perfectly cooked noodles. The bucatini was lite and had an excellent amount of seasoning. The penne pasta and squid ink pasta were both very filling. We were served very quickly. All in all, was a great meal and time celebrating Bar Primi!

Made reservations at this gem after eyeing it for a while. Beyond surpassed my expectations, literally my mouth is watering at the thought of the meal I had here.
I arrived early to my reservation as was immediately seated. Our waiter was prompt and very nice. I ordered the spaghetti and clams which was in my opinion top 2 best spaghetti and clams I've ever ate. The touch of 'nduja was the punch my pasta needed. It honestly was so good it made my boyfriend order the penne even though he just finished eating right before we arrived to the restaurant. In his opinion the penne reminded him of "complex adult Chef Boyardee."
The frosé was also to die for which was the perfect accompaniment to our meals.
My boyfriend loved his meal so much he wants to switch his birthday dinner party to this restaurant in July.
*which I'm secretly happy with because I'm in love with this place*

A gem. I'm floored. Was looking forward to sitting in this evening but the weather threatened rain. So I ordered my squid ink pasta to go and sipped the "botanica" at the bar while I waited. 

1) Hostesses at the door were super sweet.
2) Bartender was amazing. Wish I had gotten his name. (Just in case, Monday 6/17/19 around 4:45ish)
3) My pasta was still soooooooooooooo good when I got home about 40mins later.

This place is just a yes. Do go!!! I honestly can't wait to actually sit in to give the whole experience a try...

Came for happy hour before a dinner. Frose was great! The Rice balls were really delicious. We also got a plate of the olives which was huge. They have a decent happy hour menu so it's definitely worth stopping in. Our bartender was very nice I really enjoyed the conversation and I will definitely be back especially for the rice balls!

I'm giving this 4 stars because usually I have great experiences here, although the last time I was here it was a little weird. We asked our waitress for wine suggestions $55 and below (most bottles are over $55) and all of her suggestions were over $55. I had to ask again before she gave me a $55 range. She also messed up our order several times (forgetting items and bringing things out at the wrong time) but she was really nice so it made up for it. For appetizers we got: proscuitto, meatballs, and brussel sprouts. I get these every time we come because they are all SO good. They give you so much proscuitto, which is great, but the cheese to proscuitto ratio is NOT equal, so be prepared to order extra mozz (at a cost). The meatballs and brussel sprouts are always delicious and maybe the best I've ever had. 

For entrees we got the squid ink and crab pasta and the linguine with clams. I don't love seafood pasta, but my boyfriend does and he was blown away. Typically I get the pasta with garlic or the penne bolognese. Both are incredible and I would highly recommend.  

It was my boyfriend's birthday so we ordered dessert. The nutella sundae was good--but I would skip dessert next time and go to one of the really good ice cream places in the neighborhood (Sundaes & Cones)!!

Great ambience and nice spot for dinner with friends. I'm a big foodie and was quite honestly a bit disappointed with my pasta ... for a place that is know specifically for pasta I was expecting it to be outstanding but my pasta was way over cooked. A big disappointment. A plus was that our appetizers were all delicious.

I had an amazing time here when my girlfriends were in town! Wine selection was great (reasonably priced and delicious) and server was super knowledgeable about it. Food was excellent and we had a great corner table. Can't wait to go back, mangia!

First off let me say the hostess needs to find another job because she was just miserable!  Major attitude, no smile when greeting guest and very dismissive. Girl if you don't like your job go find another one instead of making everyone around you miserable. 
Our waiter started out good, talkative, happy, informative but once our orders were placed he completely disappeared and never came back until we were done eating. Didn't come to check on us to see if we needed anything(& we did!). We had to order drinks from another waitress since ours was MIA and she totally ripped us off!  We ordered our second bottle of wine, she poured 1 glass only since no one else needed much of a refill, took the bottle to the bar and set it aside. When we asked for our bottle they claimed it was done!  One drop of wine left!!! Seriously?!?  Called my waiter and he was insisting we drank the whole bottle when he wasn't even around to see it!  
VERY DISAPPOINTING!!!!!! 
As for the food, is was mediocre nothing special. Definitely will not be going here again and will never ever recommend it to others!!!

Good food but unfortunately had a very rude waiter.    6/7 of our meals were served. We waited for over 10 minutes as we watched the waiter talk to multiple other tables without giving us any update. When we asked him if he could check on it, he replied he "couldn't carry the plates on his head" and walked away. The last meal was eventually brought out by another server.  Like I said, good food but that waiters comment and overall unfriendliness dampered our mood.

Did I go on an off day? 

I dined in last Sunday evening with my family of 4 around 6pm. Weather was beautiful so we sat outdoors. We felt that overall the food was subpar in comparison to the very steep price we paid for the bill. We really enjoyed the squid ink pasta, but were disappointed with the rest of the items that we ordered - the others being the shrimp spicy paccheri, ricotta agnolotti (extremely small portion), and chicken al limone. Loved the frosé.

There are countless Italian gems in the city that I much rather wish I had spent my money at than Bar Primi. I had much higher expectations. 

Won't be returning for the food, HOWEVER, I might return for a quick glass of frosé!

Read past the weird, my Italian food was soo garlic-y (!?!?!) comments or the other questionable remarks because Bar Primi is wonderful.  Great for date night, girls night or a group of friends (make a rez).  The interior is super cute and romantic, and the food is amazing.  I think as Americans everyone looks for the Double Super Sized XL 3 lbs of pasta dishes and frankly - gross.  I love Italy, my family is from there, we vacation there, got married there.  Standard ravioli dish has about 6, and Bar Primi sizes their plates accordingly.  The bolognese is just like nonna made it, and my favorite dish.

NOW, if you want a Double Super Sized XL 3 lbs of pasta dish - head over to Olive Garden - they can hook you up with that ever so NOT Italian in any way shape or form - chicken alfredo you are searching for as well.

Average food 
Penne was cooked al dente, but sauce was lacking depth and flavor. 
Ricotta Crostini was good just small and overpriced. 
Meatballs were abit dry. 

Overall everything was sub par.

Bar Primi is a super trendy Italian restaurant in Soho. It is one of my favorite spots in Manhattan, and I am a repeat visitor. It's great for weekend brunch, casual drinks in their cute sidewalk seating area, or fancier dinners upstairs in the main dining area. Everything on the menu is great and reasonably priced. I love the ricotta crostini with honey and hazelnuts, and their simple spaghetti pomodoro with extra parmesan. Next time I want to try the tomato rice balls and chicken al limone. People really enjoy the frose in the summer, but I look forward to their blood orange frose in the Fall! Would highly recommend Bar Primi for any occasion.

My go-to for consistent good Italian. The drinks are awesome, the Paloma is my fav! All the apps are amazing but my favorites are the rice balls and Ricotta toast. For dinner I've had almost all the pastas and am always happy. My favorites are the garlic oil pasta (if you think it's too garlicy you just can't hang), the carbonara, and the squid ink pasta is amazing and has a great kick. The prices are reasonable and the quality is unmatched in the city. You can't go wrong!

This is my favorite restaurant in New York City. The pasta is phenomenal. The drinks and wine selection are also great, they're pricey but then again this is New York. Best bolognese I've ever had. 

The ambiance is laid back but beautiful. I come here whenever I can.
Had high expectations but this was a disappointment. Got the much-touted "The Sandwich", but the bread was soggy from the roast beef. Does not justify the price.

Delicious! Went in thinking it was restaurant week menu and it was not, that's my bad. We ended up sharing a pasta meal that was rigatoni and Ragu. I also had an aperol spritzer which was good and not too bitter for me.

So, I'll start with what a liked about Bar Primi. Service ice was good and the food was tasty. Now for what I didn't like. It's summer and it wasn't feeling fully comfortable in the restaurant even though the AC was on (not sure it was in full blast or not but, it's a big building, might have been out of the restaurants control, so I didn't factor that into why I gave the restaurant a 3 star rating). The portion of food was moderate but way overpriced. Portion sizes should have been larger. I also left still feeling hungry. So, it was kind of a mixed bag at Bar Primi, most likely wouldn't recommend it to friends.

There are two reasons why I keep coming back to Bar Primi.
- The "breakfast spaghetti". Mind-blowing. Sometimes I dream about it.
- Unlike every other popular brunch restaurant in this area, you can get actually get last-minute brunch reservations here. I am sure walk-ins are fine too. I love having this place in my back-pocket for brunch emergencies.

I've been here many times. Always a solid choice,
I had ordered meatballs togo. Meatballs were tough
Kitchen crew needs to keep them in sauce awhile longer
Or speak to their butcher. One thing I noticed with the fastest Growing category being take out or delivery. Restaurants fall short on quality control Bread
utensils napkins etc. tonight I received my food in
The bag with nothing else. I never mind paying for
Good food, but thats Bush league.

Came here for a girl's night. The place is super cute and the staff is very nice and friendly. The frose was very GOOD! Everyone loved their food. My only issue was that the portions could be a little bigger, and there was no yummy bread with olive oil like most Italian places. Despite that minor issue, we will definitely be back.

Went to lunch during restaurant week in the LES with a friend. We got there right as they open so unfortunately the froze machine was not ready yet so we ordered some other drinks which were really good and strong (forgot the name). For appetizer we had the burrata cremosa and brussel sprouts (fryer was down so we got to choose something else). The brussel sprouts were spot on! And the burrata was really good. For the main course we had the eggplant sandwich and the paccheri. The paccheri was sooooo good. Our server and the manager on duty were both amazing so friendly and smiley.

Two things I like from Bar primi are RICOTTA TOAST & FROSE! 

It's a cute restaurant in east village that isn't hard to miss. Perfect to dine in outdoor seat on a nice weather with a glass of frose. Their ricotta toast is so bomb and all my friends rave for it. Pastas are good too but nothing too special about it. Overall, I'd recommend coming if you're around the area to cool down on a sunny day.

Bummed out that Bar Primi did not live up to expectations. The ricotta crostino app my girlfriend ordered was the highlight of our entire meal and if you do go here it is a must have. I had the rice balls to start - the sauce over them was fresh, creamy, and delicious but the rice balls themselves did not stand out. 

For my pasta I had the bucatini amatriciana, which is similar to a lamb ragu sauce. This was good, but nothing to go crazy over. Also little on the pricier side at over $25. My girlfriend had the special, which was fusili in a ground prosciutto sauce, and she did not like it at all. I tried some and it was extremely bland - it tasted almost like spaghetti O's (which you should never pay $20+ for). My girlfriend, ever the pasta fiend, was hugely disappointed.

There are too many Italian restauraunts to try to justify a return trip to Bar Primi. I would recommend trying other Italian places in the area before this one

This place has good food but unfortunately the service (waitress/ors) really don't have personality or are they attentive my waitress looked like she did not care how my experience was or what I had to say . She also had an attitude... which is unacceptable I won't be back

For the longest time I've wanted to go to Bar Primi. Their Instagram account is the best food porn around. Tonite I got the chance. A table for 4. Two of us started with the $15 cocktails. They arrive looking like the barman only poured half the glass. But I'm told they were good. We ordered for the table stuffed meatballs, watermelon salad and burratta.  All fantastic. Except I'm still not sure what the meatballs were stuffed with. I ordered the carbonara because I was curious about a carbonara without eggs. And made with bacon and shredded cabbage. Yeah I gotto tell you this dish didn't work for me. The shredded cabbage never integrates properly with the other textures of the dish. The bacon slices are too big. And it's just all a bit odd. My wife ordered the clam spaghetti. Superb. And our guest had a ricotta pasta with pesto. Superb.  
The cheeses are fantastic. Look. The ambience is excellent. A beautiful space. Good lighting. Gorgeous terrace. Professional staff. It all works. It's an excellent restaurant.  But with that comes a hefty price tag. Literally. This is easily a $60+ a head meal.  I guess that's now the new normal in fashionable New York locations. But hey if you love well made expensive pasta, and good people watching this is the restaurant for you.
Terrible service, awful food and small portions. Penne bolognese had very little meat and the portion size was very small. I left hungry. Service was also terrible.

I've tried this place twice and am disappointed I didn't love it. Don't get me wrong -- this is a great spot for some inventive pasta dishes! I just wasn't WOWed.

My favorite part of my most recent meal was the ricotta toast. YUM! My meal was the special of the night -- a fusilli with an amatriciana style sauce. The pasta was pretty overdone and a little mushy, and the sauce just tasted like jar tomato sauce. I really wanted to love this place, but it just missed the mark twice, unfortunately.

Service was friendly and prompt.

Bar Primi has been on the Bowery for several years now and it has become a go to spot for solid Italian fare. At Bar Primi the pastas are really the stars of the show with only a few apps and a couple of mains. The beer, wine and cocktail selections are very good. The desserts are excellent as well and worth the calories.
Did not expect this place to be as good as it was. Linguini & spaghetti were super on point, not bland at all. Pricey but I left very satisfied

This place has mediocre pasta and prices are ridiculous. They try to upcharge you on everything. We asked for water and were charged $8 for a bottle of still water! I mean why wouldn't they just serve free water on tap? You can find much better restaurants in NYC for the price you pay here.

You want well thought out Italian - this is the joint! Lamb Bucatini Amatriciana for instance.

Lamb is cured and spiced for 8 weeks.  They use a bucatini rather than a papradel- the sauce gets sucked into the tube so you get a double hit with each bite.

Bellissimo
Good food and good atmosphere, but they gave my girlfriend regular coffee instead of the decaf she ordered after dinner.

Great vibes, great food, good drinks.

I love bar primi first off for their ricotta crostini appetizer. One of my favorites. Drizzled w truffle honey and hazelnuts and rosemary. 

Their patas change time to time but their bucatini agnolotti I love. Good place for Italian that isn't too fancy so you can go w friends or on a date etc. 

They have outdoor seating and bar seating so it's nice to have options.

We were a party  of 3 for lunch.  It was 2:50 pm. Not crowded. They forgot my Bellini. I think they forgot our entire order. We inquired after about 20 min. Server explained it takes 7 to 12 min to process an order. We scratched our collective heads. It was way past that. 20 min later it came. Server didnt comment i.e. apologize. Food was good but we lost or appetites. Now we had to rush to get to our next destination. So much for a relaxing lunch!

Ended up coming here because I messed up a reservation at a nearby restaurant, and luckily we were able to find seats at the communal table right away 

I must recommend the cheese sampling (formaggi). We tried one of each available. Having the side of honey and bread was a great combination. Each bite into the soft, creamy, decadent cheese and honey could be followed by just a little bread to soak it up. 

The special that night was veal with mushroom marsala which we opted for. One medium-sized piece and nicely breaded, but a whopping $35. We also got the fusilli which was rich and creamy, but rather average in quality. Dessert was the affogato, a scoop of gelato with espresso to pour on top - would recommend. 

Overall the food was satisfactory, service was excellent, but it was just a bit overpriced

Service: messed up our orders, so food took a while, but okay.
Food: cavatelli was great, but the ravioli was super super salty, so ended up returning by the fish for the cavatelli. 
Overall not consistent with both the food and service.

After spending some time in little Italy and deciding we can't go to one of those tourist traps we found this place online. It's really hard to mess up Italian but Bar Primi did it and we may have been better off staying in Little Italy.

We started with the anti pasta - it was fine, but had maybe two pieces of meat and cheese. We also got the toast with ricotta which was good but nothing special and I would always prefer bruschetta when eating Italian food. 

Mains.....black ink pasta with crab meat and the bucatini amatricina. I'm sorry to say this but the crab meat pasta lasted like a bland version of my moms tuna and noodle casserole. How can you do that to a beautiful ingredient like crab? Bucatini was better for sure. The sauce was nice but it just lacked flavor or anything to make it special in the sea of Italian food that we have in NY. I generally love amatricina but really, who invented bucatini in the first place? 

And then we got dessert because we didn't want to go wander around. The hazelnut Sunday was pretty good. The chocolate tasted like a melted kinder bar and was so tasty! Panna cotta again lacked depth and flavor. They put a ton of sliced almonds and fruit on top as well, maybe to make up for the lack of flavor in the panna cotta itself? 

I also did not have a napkin for the mains or dessert, we ordered two cappuccinos with a shot of bourbon and had finished our coffees before the bourbon even came out. 

Overall, not a great experience overall and will definitely be looking elsewhere for my Italian food.

MANHATTAN/Bowery: a stop on Petminded's dog restaurant week tour was Bar Primi! Dogs are allowed at their lush and pretty outdoor space. Dogs are always allowed at the outdoor tables, but for dog restaurant week, the restaurant gave a $5 donation to Bideawee.org, a no-kill animal shelter, and all dogs received a complimentary tennis ball!

The Italian food was delicious and it's always a good sign when there's a line to dine! Very popular place!

Can't say enough good things about my entire evening at Bar Primi. The entire meal from start to finish was delicious. We celebrated my boyfriends birthday and the staff went out of their way to make the night a little extra special. We split an assortment of cheeses and the Brooklyn arugula salad to start. Both were wonderful. For our main course we ordered the linguine with 4 cloves of garlic and breadcrumbs and the penne bolognese. Both dishes set the bar very high for pasta dinners in Manhattan. We didn't leave a single scrap of food behind. It was a nice evening with great wine and even better food. We will most definitely be back

DELICIOUS brunch. Great service, location, quantities, price... We'll definitely be returning.
We got the ricotta crostino as well but ate it too quickly to take a photo, it was that good.
Our entrees (breakfast spaghetti and baked eggs pomodoro) were unique and incredible. Can't recommend this place enough
Phenomenal food- highly recommend the rice balls and to be honest any pasta dish. We were a group of 6 and everyone's pasta was amazing. Service was great as well. Cannot wait to go back.

I came here for dinner the other night after trying to find an Italian place to go to since my cousin was in town. I live right down the street from this restaurant and walk by it every single day but never had a chance to go. I saw they had a reservation on open table the day of so I went ahead and secured us a spot. I got there early, had a glass of wine at the bar and waited for everyone to get there. We were seated upstairs which had such a great vibe and was very energetic. It's a beautiful space but still low key. We ordered the meatballs and ricotta toast to start- both were delicious. For our mains, we each ordered a pasta since that's what the restaurant is known for. I had the pomodoro with gluten free pasta which was good and the other pastas we ordered were the rigatoni carbonara and the penne bolognese. Everyone said they enjoyed their dishes. For dessert, we had the Nutella sundae which was great. Everything from the ambiance to the food and wine was great. If you're looking for a relaxed spot to have some comfort food/pasta this is a great place.

I came here to catch up with my girlfriends and although the bill came out to be a bit pricey (which is my only con of my visit) I still highly suggest this spot for anyone who wants a special romantic/intimate evening with their loved ones. 

Things that made me happy for my visit:
-Homemade al dente pasta (SO YUM) (only short pastas are homemade)
-Dairy free options available and they're willing to accommodate (come through my lactose intolerant friends) 
-$3 PLATE OF OLIVES!!! For happy hour only but still. This plate was bigger than my head. And I had leftovers I took home to enjoy. 
-$1 meatballs woot woot
-Happy hour priced negroni that I could drink all darn night. 
-Smiling faces from all the staff the entire time!

I'll be back!!

I've generally found Andrew Carmellini's other restaurants to feel a bit too commercial so it wasn't too surprising that this place had a similar vibe. The food was generally fine and the salad was genuinely very good. The menu was very simple which is presumably a feature, not a bug.

Came in last night for a quick and casual dinner with my husband. The food was delicious - but what truly made the evening spectacular was our server Jessica. Jessica killed it - attentive, bubbly, and all the way on top of it. - Her skill was amplified when the table next to us became very difficult and borderline rude. - Jessica remained cool, calm, collected - and most impressively kind to them. - THANK YOU! - will be back. Will be back with friends and family.

We came here with my wife's recommendation from real housewives...... the location was decent with a bar on the first floor and  lots of tables upstairs. We split the kale salad, which is plenty for 2, to start with. It tasted good but nothing out of the ordinary. I was craving lasagna, which they don't serve. Instead I chose their lamb pasta  and my friend got linguini. Both dishes had good flavor and the pasta itself tasted great! And homemade.

We had a bad experience at Bar Primi earlier this year and posted a negative review, which we rarely do but had a really uncomfortable service experience so felt compelled to. The Bar Primi mgmt reached out to rectify the situation and offered us a complimentary dinner on them. Even though we insisted we'd be back again despite poor service one time, they were adamant we come in for the meal.


We are so blown away - the service, food, atmosphere, and generosity is fantastic. We got the ricotta toast with truffle honey & hazelnuts to start, and then split the hangar steak with garlic linguine. To die for!! 

I have always loved this restaurant and am so appreciative that one bad experience won't be my lasting impression. The lengths the ownership have gone to to prove to us that they value our patronage is really incredible. Thank you, Bar Primi! We love you and will be back again!

I literally dream of their pasta! I visit NYC twice a year and always make a point to stop here for dinner. I tend to eat dinner a bit earlier than most in NYC so I don't ever have an issue grabbing a table.

If you're looking for brunch and you're too hungover to fathom the thought of eggs, this is your spot. Fantastic pasta options with gluten free noodles available. I suggest ordering pasta for yourself, then eating the truffle omelet off of your boyfriends plate once your hangover has subsided.

Great food and great service. I appreciate when a server is knowledgeable about everything on the menu. I had one food restriction and he was very accommodating. There were 5 of us and we all had a different pasta. Everyone's food looked delicious!

One of my favorite Italian restaurant finds this year. I've come for multiple meals and really loved it every time. It is on the pricier side, but I do think they have great dishes that make it more justifiable than other places might be.

In the summer, they have outdoor seating that is super pleasant, but the restaurant also has two floors of seating space if you want to dine indoors

Their Squid Ink is one of my favorite pastas BY FAR. It's creamy and has a generous portion of crab, so if that's up your alley then go for it. Do note it's not available on their brunch menu sadly.

All of their tomato sauce pastas are delish too, as are the meatballs. But if you're not feeling a pasta for brunch, I also love their Meatballs and Polenta dish. It's super filling and just feels hearty.

For some reason they are also known for their frose. While it is good (and quite alcoholic-tasting), there's really nothing special about it to me.

Wonderful staff and great food. If I lived closer to Bar Primi it would be one of my regular dinner spots. The restaurants has seat on the first and second floor plus seat at the bar(a given). I prefer to sit at the bar as it has enough space. I like the spaghetti with clams and sometimes go for the Branzino. For drinks, the bartenders can make this delicious Rose Old Fashion. 

I believe they do not take reservations but provide delivery for those that like to sit at home. Bar Primi is worth multiple trips and a new personal fav.

Came here for a birthday dinner and they were very accommodating of our giant group. The pasta dishes were great, and portion sizes were filling without overdoing it (just enough to leave you wanting more). The cocktail menu was also good and the server was very warm and friendly. Would definitely go back to try more of the menu. It's a cozy venue that manages to be good for groups, which can be hard to find.

A place with passable food and poor value for the price. I got the squid ink pasta and my friend got the steak. The food was ok, nothing remarkably good or bad. But one drink and one tiny portion of pasta barely larger than an appetizer ran me 60 after tip. No idea how that price point made it on the bib gourmand list.
The food was okay and the service was okay. Not bad but I wouldn't come again. Not worth a shot

Came here with my boyfriend for date night. The seating was strange because I sat on the inside of the table which was a booth type thing with cushion and it made me sink in and look smaller on the table. While the other side was a regular chair and my boyfriend sat tall.

Anyways, aside from that the food was really good and so was the wine we ordered

The short: amazing food, nice wine list, lovely ambiance -- but really confusing dinner service. 

The longer: I arrived with a friend on a Monday night for a 7:30 pm dinner reservation. Though it wasn't even that crowded, it took us at least 15 minutes to be seated. 

So, we grabbed seats and wine at the bar. We had to remind them that we'd arrived. Wine was great. 

We had a seat upstairs, and had two different waitresses - both very nice. We ordered Brussels sprouts, the prosciutto and two pasta entrees. The appetizers were amazing. The Brussels come with pepperonis and are perfectly cooked. The portion of prosciutto is massive, and it's well seasoned with sea salt and topped with fresh mozzarella. 

Both of our pasta entrees were also delicious. I highly recommend the fiore di carciofi. It's different and incredibly well done. My friend's bolognese was very good, too. 

But, they brought me out the wrong pasta. So, we ate our dinners separately - which is unfortunate and unexpected at a restaurant of their caliber. They apologized but didn't do anything to make amends. We didn't make a big deal of it - but was disappointing and would make me think twice about returning.
