Had brunch at Bar Primi recently. We were there right when it opened so it wasn't crowded by any means. The service was pretty good, but not great. The ambiance is cute, cozy, and trendy. The food was just really really average though. We did the ricotta crostini to start which was the best dish. My carbonara was oily and had started to separate. Not worth it at all.
Appetizer and desserts were awesome! But the pastas were lil disappointing. The flavors arent that great at all. But the atmosphere of the place is good for all occasions.
Came for a work lunch - the lunch special $29 for an appetizer and main is a pretty good deal! The kale salad and carbonara were both delicious and extremely filling. I'm a fan!

Food here is very good and the place itself is very nice and rustic. We were here for NYE and the kitchen was a bit slow but service was attentive and the food was well cooked. There are so many quality Italian places in the area but Bar Primi is definitely one of the better spots and would recommend for those looking for a nice Italian meal with some very good wine.

Went for restaurant week deal and it did not disappoint! The burrata and cacio e pepe appetizer were amazing! Great way to start the meal. Loved both. Then the two trofie pasta which was like a white bolognese sauce was AMAZING, could of eaten it all. The cacio e pepe was more just like buttered noodles? No cheese which was a let down. Both desserts were light and a great way to finish off the meal as well! Cute ambiance too.

So I first thought that this place was participating in restaurant week on Saturdays, but it didn't matter when I found out it did not: the food was splendid and the ambience was SO nice. 

We ordered a glass of red wine and rosé. The wine was very full-bodied and rich, which I appreciate a lot. Anyway, the burrata was so creamy and silky, it was such an amazing appetizer. It melts right in your mouth. The two pastas we ordered paired so well with each other. The squid ink pasta was the right amount of chewiness and had small pieces of crab in it. The shrimp in the spicy paccheri was so juicy. Loved this place. 

Would definitely come back again!

Two stars, one for wonderful server who took care of us and one for the ricotta panna cotta which was delicious. Everything else I did not like. We had the kale insalata which was okay, the burrrata - which needed more peppers, the stuffed meatballs- which were way too salty. For dinner we ordered the bucatini that had the lamb way overcooked, the spaghetti pomodoro- which was sweet and confusing.. and the cacio e Pepe spaghetti which was WAY TOO SALTY. For dessert the tiramisu was okay, the hazelnut gelato was okay and the  panna cotta was to die for. Don't think I'd come here again as it was a bit pricey for all the mistakes the food had but if you find yourself here, have panna cotta and avoid the other foods mentioned.

Currently here for restaurant week. 
Although the bartender was above and beyond for service and quality, the waiter and co. was something else to be desired.  Aside from the blatant attitudes given, the waiter was quite condescending to our party. I wish I could conclude it was due to us drinking; however, we had just come from work and hadn't even begun the dinner crowd, which we questionably had to obtain a dinner table - keep in mind the entire restaurant was still empty because it was only 5pm.  The dinner portions and quality themselves were minuscule, especially for the price point.  After seeing why they presently had a 3.5 star rating, I can clearly understand. 
The only reason I'm giving them a 2 star is because the drinks and bartender were delicious and pleasant.
I friggin love this place. I don't know what else to say. One of my favorite spots in the city. Everything on the menu is great. Service can be a little slow when busy, but it's worth it!!

First time coming by my friend & I just stopped by for drinks , we sat at the bar & gave the Frose a try ahh I have to say not really a fan $16 dollars for a half full glass ? What gives!! Taste wise it's not terrible but for the price tag it's not really worth it.
Next time around we gave the food a try during restaurant week, we started with a suggested glass of white wine, very nice. 
Appetizers we had the Cauliflower cacio e pepe now this is one way to get me to eat cauliflower loll... this was very good, crispy cauliflower great sauce it was very tasty. the Burrata cremosa was delicious nice big piece of Burrata cheese so good great combo with the bread. 
Main dishes we tried the Spaghetti cacio e pepe so simple yet so tasty this was sooo good also had the Chicken mushroom marsala , nice juicy pieces of chicken, great tasting sauce. 
For Dessert the Gelato was great, nice almond taste very good the Riccota panna costa is not bad did like the berries & honey taste. 
Decent size restaurant they have two levels which we initially did not notice, nice & casual below along with the bar area seems a bit more intimate upstairs where we sat. Service was good our waiter was so nice & attentive. good prices due to restaurant week decent with out food was very good & it was definitely worth the try.
My boyfriend and I went on a date here. It was a lovely, dark, and moody atmosphere, and the staff was very friendly. The food was delicious. I would recommend for a date night.

What a great experience. Food was great. Drinks were delicious... but most importantly, our service was out of this world. We stopped at the bar to grab a drink while we waited for our table. The bartender was welcoming and answered all of questions. Our waitress, Meredith, made our night. She had such a great personality! We would go back tomorrow  if she's guaranteed to be our waitress. Highly recommend!

We came here for dinner for my first New York experience. I had the Squid ink Campanella--crab meat, creamy sauce and Fresno chili. I loved it. The waiter also recommended a great red wine for me (not much of a red wine drinker) but I couldn't be happier. 
Now I am in the process of trying to find this recipe  so so good. 

RECOMMEND 100/10

My biggest pet peeve is having a reservation for a place and still having to wait... THIS WAS NOT WHAT WE EXPERIENCED HERE. We went there at prime time and we were still seated within a reasonable time frame. The hostess was very kind and asked us to wait by the bar. The servers were very attentive and made us feel welcomed. The food is great. We had two appetizers and two pastas. Portions were reasonable and they came out at a steady pace. All in all a good experience.

Best Italian I have had in the city - pasta is so fresh and the sauces are the best. Only downside to this place is that the drinks are to expensive and the plates are a little small. All made up for with flavor and taste though!

Bar Primi is such a gem!  What a cozy & charming restaurant.  Love the Sal's Antipasti Salad, always a must order! The pasta's are always fantastic & great to share.  Love the Chicken Al Limone. Be sure to save room for the tiramisu!

Order takeout from this place via Postmates.  The squid ink pasta with crabmeat was absolutely incredible. Staff was very friendly and the place was absolutely packed when I came to pick up my order. Vibe seemed great so I'll be sure to make a reservation and bring some people along next time.

Worst then ever use to be my favorite spot never again will i go back there something happened there its not the same!!! 30 dollars for the smallest bowl of macaroni that cost 1 dollar to make !!!!!!! Please do not waste your money or time!!! Its a has been ---used to

Italian but with limited pasta options, also limited 2nd course options. Ordered an arugula salad and instead of goat cheese, raisins?! Not a good combination in my view. Pastas were ok. Been to better italians in the region and with a bettee cost/benefit.

Went  here for brunch the other day funny story I actually got it confused with quotes Italian restaurant with a similar name I want to order this specific pasta dish that they are famous for .so when i showed up and realized they didn't have it on the menu I was EXTREMELY disappointed. ... until my food came out we were extremely happy with what we ordered . The fresh linguine with 4 cloves of garlic and breadcrumbs was fantastic.  It was packed with flavored and wanted us wanting more . We also enjoyed the stuffed meatballs with the Italian red marinara sauce.
Bar Primi is a nice and cozy Italian joint, serving it's own homemade pasta. The squid ink pasta was good with a little kick and the spaghetti pomodora was a classic and scrumptious staple.

So glad to have stumbled upon this spot while being on the waitlist somewhere else. It was a cute corner restaurant spot. We had a quick dinner so we just ordered pasta. We LOVED the squid ink pasta!
The staff was friendly and accommodating. Since we were sitting outside there was no issues having dinner with the pooch!
Great  restaurant and addition to the neighborhood. Love their pasta selection and wine. We always love their food. Could sue outdoor heaters, but appreciate the outdoor eating option.

Well here goes the yelp delivery review you may never expect, but so glad it's here! :Cheesy post alert: 

Due to COVID-19, my (now husband) and I were supposed to have a beach summer wedding on LI. Instead we chose to postpone the whole thing, and get married legally over zoom 2 months ago. Now what is my point for telling this, well... we ordered from this place of course!! We liked it so much, my husband surprised me and ordered from here again :). Everything was so delicious, gluten free pasta was on point. So satisfying and really added to out special occasions the last few months. Bar Primi will be forever in our hearts!

We came here for New Year's Eve dinner and despite the pandemic, restaurant restrictions, and early closing, Bar Primi was able to make it as festive as they possibly could. They started off the night with complimentary bubbly glasses and each table had its own heater - I was toasty in my dress! The staff was very attentive for our drink and appetizer orders and service was quick. My garlic pasta was a delicious elevated version of a basic aglio olio, and the bolognese was also delicious. However, the cheeses are a star of the show here with the drinks. I could have been satisfied with the ricotta toasts, burrata, cheese plates, and my whiskey cocktails. It was a great way to bid adieu in a quiet, intimate setting to a challenging year. 

Note: If anyone in your party has a shellfish allergy, the options are limited since their standouts all contain seafood/shellfish.

Came in to Bar Primi last Thursday for dinner with a friend. We didn't make reservations and showed up at 6:30 with no problems with getting a table. BUT it did fill up significantly by the time we left around 7:45. So if you are going later, I would suggest a reservation. They also have an hour and a half dining limit which totally makes sense! It was plenty of time for us to eat and enjoy. 

Our waitress was very attentive. They have a great outdoor set up with heaters next to all the tables. It wasn't too bad out that night (low 40s) and we were extremely comfortable! I was even able to take off my jacket. 

It was SO difficult to decide what to get! So many good looking options. I was torn between the carbonara and the bolognese (because of the ricotta on top). I decided on the carbonara because I've actually never tried that kind of pasta before! Wow! I was impressed. Huge pieces of bacon and the cabbage was an excellent addition! My friend got the sweet potato brown butter agnolotti. Ohhh it was divine!! For sure recommend this spot!

My boyfriend and I came here last night for Valentines' Day. Our table was for 6:15, and it was ready exactly at that time. We sat indoors, and once inside they have clear plastic barriers in between each table which was nice. The drinks were good I got the frosè and him a beer. Both tasty. For food we got the stuffed meatballs which were sooooo yummy. It comes with 4 covered in sauce (no photos cause we were starving lol), and for our entrees I got the squid ink pasta with garlic cream sauce and crab. If you like creamy pasta dishes this is for you! My boyfriend got the hanger steak which comes with potatoes and a arugula salad. Also very very yummy! Of course we had to get dessert, and we got the tiramisu. Super tasty, it was a little heavy on the powder they put over it, but it was so moist so it kinda cancelled it out. Overall great food and service, would for sure come back here!

Loved the ambiance, my BF and I sat indoors on Valentine's Day. The tables were spread out and we felt safe. They have a lot of gluten free options including any of the pastas. The grilled octopus is superb as well

When your BFF says we have to get the ricotta crostini, you trust her! We went all in for Saturday brunch, only making it home by 11pm 
The penne bolognese and breakfast pasta were crowd pleasers in our group & I was also impressed with our bloody mary's. 

Indoor dining seemed to only be happening upstairs, but there were lots of people over the winter blues and enjoying a meal upstairs and indoors. The staff at Bar Primi seemed to be covid cautious by informing us to remain 6' apart while waiting for the bathroom (which is what I like to see!) 

I will definitely add Bar Primi to the list of usual suspects for brunch.

My boyfriend and I came to Bar Primi on a cold winter's day for a late brunch. We ordered the Brussels sprouts, breakfast spaghetti and the rigatoni with tomatoes and eggplant. The pasta dishes were solid but not as memorable as some my other favorites in the city. The Brussels sprouts were cooked with pepperoni and topped generously with Parmesan cheese. This rendition was one of the best I've ever had and something I would love to try to recreate at home.

I would not hesitate to return again if I wanted a casual dinner in the area. It seems that some of their more famous pasta dishes are offered only at dinner so I am looking forward to trying those and perhaps will review again when I do that.

One of the best meals I've had in awhile. Thr meal was delicious from beginning to end. We dined on Stuffed Meatballs, Penn Bolognese, Spaghetti and Clams amd Tiramisu. The Bolognese was amazing. The sauce was not overly salty or acidic. It was great combination if flavors and nicely coated the fresh pasta. Same for the Spaghetti and Clams. Definitely get th e tiramisu. Absolutely delicious. The servixe was also top notch and covid safe

We had a great time celebrating my daughter's birthday at Bar Primi! On a beautiful Saturday afternoon in March, we dined outdoors here for brunch. The setup outside is perfect and the staff was very friendly. 

We all thought the food was fantastic! I started off with an IPA from Three's Brewery in Gowanus (which we had brunch at a few years ago). We split the burrata cremosa appetizer which was amazing! For entrees, my daughter and I both ordered Meatballs with polenta. This dish served with sunny side up eggs and grilled bread was so good! I loved the meatballs! My wife had Pancakes and thought they were phenomenal!

This is a really popular spot in the lower East Side. Make reservations and enjoy this great restaurant!

A friend of mine suggested we try bar primi for dinner this week and I'm so glad he did- the food was outstanding. The bolognese with ricotta was unreal, and my friend had the linguine and added clams to it, which looked delicious as well.  Only negative I would say would be that the menu is pretty limited, it didn't seem like there were a ton of options.  Overall, the food was great and the staff were all super attentive and friendly, I will definitely be back!

If you're coming here for the frosè because allegedly this is where it was "invented" (lmao some 17 year old mixing odd ingredients with Absolut vodka was well ahead of you, but go off), then I'm doing you a favor and telling you: don't go. First of all, they will serve the frosè with a pasta straw. That pasta could have been used to cook some fine dining for a starch g family or the same homeless man who sits outside during weekdays. Just use a recyclable paper straw like everyone else, it's disgusting and not cute. Also the food here is just painfully average for the price. Maybe go with the meatballs if you're just coming for the drinks, I don't really know.
Loved eating here! I will def be returning. Huge inside restaurant and fun atmosphere, pasta and chicken were flavorful and drinks were tasty.

Pretty good food, went here for my girlfriend's birthday. 

Bit pricey but high quality and not that bad for downtown. 

Fully COVID safe (proper outdoor seating without enclosed walls but with a ceiling and heater, masks, etc)

A perfect spot for an amazing meal & a frozen drink in warm weather. Reservations are recommended as they get busy pretty quickly!

Bar Primi's dinner has options for everyone, we went with the recomendable meatless options by our server & everything was to die for. 

Their frozé is strong & delicious -- fun fact their straws are actually cooked pasta sticks which made the experience fun & memorable! 

To start we had the Sicilian tomato rice balls (not pictured) they tasted like a mouthful of a lasagna literally amazing. & The burrata which was so fresh & yummy.

Our entrees were the Spaghetti Pomodoro & the Ricotta Agnolotti and both were amazing my favorite out of the two was the ravioli because it was extra cheese & creamy.

& If you haven't had gelato before I would def give it a go, the almond one was topped w roasted nuts & it was perfect!

Can't wait to go back & keep trying new things!

This was the WORST and SALTIEST linguine I have ever had. I took one bite and could not take another because it wasn't edible. It tasted as if half of a salt bottle was poured into this dish.. do yourself a favor and spend your $25 somewhere else because it was not worth any of my penny for this type of dish.. I asked why it was so salty and they replied saying it's suppose to be this salty.. don't trust how it looks!! Looks are deceiving!! Never going back! My friends were all disappointed and only took one bite of it for $25 each...I would rate this 0/5 stars if I could!!

We got the burrata, squid ink campanelle, and grilled branzino. The campanelle was awesome, soft briny noodles with plenty of crabmeat and chilis for a kick. The burrata was just ok -- could have been richer with a creamier texture. The branzino was a small, lightly seasoned portion that was pretty unsatisfying for the price. The italian sodas are surprisingly good.

Bar Primi Ratings: 4.1/5

Food: 4.5/5 - I am a huge pasta fan!!! I have tried so many pasta places in the city, and I would say I approve of this Italian restaurant. I ordered a Soave as my drink, and it was the closest drink I can find similar to a Chardonnay. For pasta, I got the Squid Ink Campanelle. It was chewy, rich, and super creamy with a good amount of crab meat. The crab was fresh, and the pepper on the top definitely added a good kick of spice to it for a change of flavor. Love the dish. I didn't give 5 star review, because I thought the pasta could be a bit more flavorful or saltier? Also, they did not provide any free bread as starter, which I was so sad about because I really love some free CARBS. This is probably the only pasta place I been to that didn't offer free bread. 

Ambiance: 4/5 - First, the vibe was really good and the outdoor seating set up was super cute, perfect for dates. The down side was that there was only outdoor seating available, and honestly it was a bit too hot in NYC, so I was sweating my butt off eating pasta, very not comfortable, but the pasta made it worth it. 

Price: 4/5 - Overall, the food quality was good. I would say the price was slightly high for the amount of food given. The pasta was around $27 and the drink was $15. 

Service: 3.75/5 - They have done a good job practicing social distancing, using clear dividers to separate each table and staffs were wearing masks too. The only bad thing was that the service was a bit slow, maybe because it was packed or our server was just not attentive enough? 

BLUF: At the end of the day, if you are visiting NYC or in LES, you should try out this place! I love their squid ink pasta and would love to go back to try out the Bolognese pasta next time, heard good reviews about that. Would recommend to visit when they open indoor seating.

My boyfriend and I came here for our anniversary dinner. The food was fantastic - flavorful and classic. The pasta was cooked perfectly and the cocktails were delicious. 

Unfortunately, the service wasn't great. Our server was very friendly but service was just...slow. It took 15 minutes for us to be acknowledged at the table. Once we placed orders, it seemed to pick up. But then once we needed a check, again...slow. 

The food and cocktails were so great, we'd definitely come back with the hope that service would be better.
Food was great, service felt a little rushed. Outdoor seating is tight as well. Would come back!
Came here for a Saturday brunch. It was a chill, laid back vibe which I liked. The food was decent, but didn't blow me away.

Beautiful spot in NOHO for dinner. We sat outside and although it was hot, the weather was beautiful at dusk. We shared the Brussels sprouts which were UNREAL (best I've ever had) and I got the Penne, which was so fresh and filling. Wonderful service and atmosphere!

Great food! 
The burrata was very creamy and the bread it came with was delicious as well.
The squid ink pasta was amazing. It had a bit of a spice that really added to the dimension of the flavor and complimented the crab meat.
The stuffed meatballs were flavorful and a good portion too!
The spaghetti Pomodoro was cooked perfectly al dente. Adding a little Parmesan definitely went a long way, but you cannot go wrong with this classic.
The octopus was awesome! My friend was raving about the pesto on top of it.
Overall: My friends and I enjoyed the food and had a good time at this lovely spot on the Bowery!

LOVE this spot for a casual dinner with a fun atmosphere and good Italian food. We ordered the prosciutto and mozzarella to start, which had perfectly thin shaved prosciutto that just melts in your mouth. Our table also had the squid ink pasta and the garlic linguine for entrees and the tiramisu for dessert. We got the garlic linguine with gluten free pasta, which is one of the better gluten free pastas we've had in the city. It's nice that there's no extra charge for it!

The food was quite nice but the service was absolutely terrible. We had a 9pm reservation... Our table wasnt ready for 30 minutes so they sat us at the bar. Because of the inconvenience, they offered cocktails on the house, which was a lie as it was on my bill. We finally got sat down and then did not see a waiter for another 15 minutes. He finally came over and did not introduce himself, thank us for waiting, nor tell us anything about the menu/restaurant. Instead he just said "Are there any questions?". He made no attempt to even act like a waiter and was one of the least personable waiters i have had in NYC. Plain and simple, he was rude. He acted as if I was doing something wrong for being the customer and spending well over $200. I will not hurry back as there are so many other restaurants in NYC that are actually appreciate of their patrons business. I think the food was good enough to maybe try it again in the future, but the service was boarderline offensive.
We went for dinner on a slow Sunday yet the wait staff was inattentive and couldn't be found. The appetizers were good but the pasta was mediocre.
$16 for a SVEDKA cosmo? SVEDKA??????? I haven't had SVEDKA since I was 17!!! Just made your small over-priced pasta dish taste worse. Also the waiter was rude. Bye.

Came here for dinner with a friend. I made a reservation through Resy, but when I arrived, they weren't able to locate it. Luckily, we were still able to get seated outside but just a fair warning if you book this place through Resy. My friend opted for the restaurant week dinner menu which was caprese and chicken marsala for $39. I was bummed they didn't have another restaurant week option with pasta, but ended up getting the penne along with frosé. Overall, all of the food was good. Definitely want to come back to try some of the other items. Found the service to be a bit lacking though. It took a long time for our order to be taken and also took a while to get the check. They may be short-staffed because of COVID which is understandable. Recommend this place if you're looking for solid Italian food with a nice ambiance.

I definitely wish their menu had more options - even if just traditional. A lot of their pasta combinations didn't make sense. Bacon and cabbage in one, for example. Also, their pasta menu is predominantly red meat heavy which I'm not a big fan of. 
The ravioli I ordered was really good though. Burrata was good and super soft. Came with peppers that gave it a nice touch. Also ordered the crostini, the ricotta was so good, but they topped it with hazelnuts and truffle honey which wasn't as bad as I expected but also wasn't my favorite. I think it could have done without the additional crunch and sweetness. 
The tiramisu was a classic dessert choice - super soaked ladyfingers, just the way I like it so no complaints there.
Loved the food, had friendly staff staff and the restaurant was spacious - which happens to be important during these times.

Wow! What a great experience! We were in the city to send my brother off to college and were blown away with the food, service, atmosphere, and so much more. Carlos was our server and did a phenomenal job! Will definitely be back.

I'll start off saying I've only had brunch at Bar Primi, although multiple times, and the food is always delicious and consistent. 

Brunch doesn't have to mean eggs and pancakes, although their brunch menu does have those options, and sometimes I'm craving fresh homemade pasta with my mimosa at noon on a Sunday. If your cravings align it's a great spot to bring guests for a more casual brunch. I always enjoy the cozy but bright atmosphere (outdoor or indoor), and it's on the border of NoHo and East Village so it's a good area to be situated in if you want to roam (or continue drinking) afterwards! Their breakfast spaghetti is especially a delicious take on a brunch-esque carbonara. Also you can get pitchers of mimosas on a variety of flavors and who doesn't love that.

4 stars not 5 because although its a convenient, consistent place for a brunch reservation with relatively yummy pasta, I wouldn't go out of my way to eat there if I was craving top notch pasta given all the other options in the city. The service also tends to be on the slower side. I'll have to try some more dishes for dinner and maybe I'll have to update this review!

I went on a Sunday for a late brunch. There was plenty of outdoor seating and the setup was pretty nice and covered with fans as well. The 2 pasta dishes we had were great! But I favored the linguine a bit more than the penne, it had more texture from the bread crumbs and was nice and light. The penne was more substantial, but nothing out of the ordinary aside from the cheese that came with it. The cheese was very smooth and made the dish almost creamy with every bite. What I liked most about bar primi was that I didn't struggle to make a reservation for brunch like at some places and the food was pretty tasty. The portions at least for the penne specifically could have been a bit bigger, but overall it met my expectations. I would recommend giving bar primi a try and I'll go back again for dinner eventually.

Bar Primi was a cute spot that wasn't overly populated by any means at the bar top! My friend recommended we stop in for some drinks on our way to dinner on the lower East Side. The drinks were decent, though seemed a bit pricey for quality in the end. I ordered the Brosé which was very sweet/slushy and also came in a smaller portion. It tasted good though I don't know if I would order it again as it seemed more like a desert and less like an alcoholic beverage. My friend's beverage was closer to an aperol spritz which I enjoyed, but also seemed very sweet from their signature cocktail list. The staff are incredibly friendly, attentive, and the bar was super clean! I would love to come back and give their food a try. Their cocktails were truly not bad, just a bit too sweet for my taste with a high dollar sign attached.

Oh. My. God! This is my third time returning to Bar Primi and it won't be my last. After being told we would need to wait 3 hours for a table at a restaurant nearby, we walked a few short steps when we stumbled upon Bar Primi and the lightbulbs went off! I'd visited previously for restaurant week and really enjoyed the food, so I was so happy when we walked in around 7:30 PM on Friday and were able to sit immediately. Started off with frosé (which I believe originated at Bar Primi?) and later switched to a Basílico cocktail which was very refreshing. For appetizers my partner and I ordered the grilled octopus, as well as prosciutto and mozzarella. The octopus was tender with a nice char. The mashed potatoes weren't perfect but hey I'm not coming to an Italian place for their potatoes. Didn't get a picture of the prosciutto and mozzarella but wow it was a huge portion! A mountain of meat with a nice drizzle of olive oil, and some salt and pepper. We were a little disappointed it didn't come with bread but no harm no foul, we ordered some and it was nice and soft and chewy. When it came time for the entree, we both opted for the squid ink crab campanelle. Absolutely no regrets about that! It came in a garlicky, creamy sauce and was perfectly cooked. I had a few pieces left when I put my fork down because I was feeling full and said that I was done. Well, two minutes later I picked up my fork again and cleared my plate. Service was also incredible. Our friendly and funny server checked in on us multiple times and was always accessible. We didn't have room for dessert but had previously enjoyed it during restaurant week! I look forward to my next visit.

Came here to try their garlic linguine with breadcrumbs but was honestly disappointed. The linguine was just drowned in oil and tasted nothing special. There was a bit of garlic flavor but that was as far as the flavor went. A bit too simple to be a signature dish in my opinion.

Great place of choice when other nearby restaurants are an hour+ long waits.

This place has extensive amount of seats. Pretty good service , food was cute. Nothing super exciting, but definitely a great warm meal when your famished. Thank you :)
Liked the place - it was busy but staff was attentive.  Good GF option - pasta sauce was really good.  Also dessert was very nice.  Fun place.  Recommended for casual dining.

Food and service here are both good. Lots of good pasta selections. Two are house made -- the orecchiette and the agnolotti. Both were very good. The arugula salad with dried cherries, almonds, caprino was good too. Service was friendly, efficient and helpful. The restaurant is right next to the Bowery Hotel.

Pepperoni Brussels sprouts. Squid ink pasta. Tiramisu. This is my standard order at Bar Primi and it never disappoints. The pasta particularly is fantastic and I recommend this spot to all my friends who come to visit and they all LOVE it. Highly recommend!

Cute & cozy bar! Great for a date night or to grab a drink at the bar! The bartender was quick & friendly. As a vegetarian I was pleased to have this tasty ricotta crositino with hazelnuts & truffle honey. The truffle honey was the best! Combined with a glass of champagne and it was a relaxing evening at the bar. Indoor & outdoor seating available.

What an amazing meal! I was so stuffed by the end, I couldn't even finish my main dish. I went to Bar Primi last night with 4 other friends. The ambiance is great. Nice lighting- not too bright, but not too dark. We started off with the ricotta toast and the rice balls. I would definitely recommend the rice balls over the ricotta toast. I love truffle, however, the honey on the toast made it too sweet and almost dessert like. Still good, but I don't think it's what we were looking for in terms of apps. We then each got a pasta. Below are photos of the penne bolognese, squid ink campanelle, ricotta agnolotti, and the fusilli. All were delicious, however, after having a bite of each I think the bolognese and squid ink were the winners. Squid ink is very rich though- beware!! Along with our meal we had a few glasses of wine that were delicious and heavy pours as well. Highly recommend this place! Good for date night or nice dinner with friends. Nice service as well.
Went to Bar Primi with friends. Foods and vibes are really good. Love the squid ink campanelle and Burrata with bread.  Spaghetti is delicious too!

Absolutely disgusting experience. Had a reservation yet left my party waiting for 40 minutes. We sat there and watched the white waiters take the order of other white people that came much later than us while we were not helped during that entire duration... We were left starving so ended up walking out instead of having to deal with this bullshit. Funny how we weren't assisted at all and right when I walked out the door, the waiter cancelled our reservation and I received the email notification. Disgusting that's when they decide to finally acknowledge us. This was supposed to be a special dinner but they definitely were the worst possible start to the night. Would not recommend if you are looking to get treated right or looking for a nice ambiance of any sort.

The food was good, but not "spit in my face" good. The service wasn't great, we actually saw another group leave before ordering drinks. 

I'd probably order from here and take it to go next time.

We came in hoping for comforting Italian food, and were not disappointed! 

We started with an order of the Sicilian Tomato Rice Balls and of the Brussel Sprouts - both were very flavorful and filling. A stand-out aspect for me was the texture of the Brussel Sprouts - the thicker, outer leaves were surprisingly crunchy!

Texture was another highlight when we ordered the Rigatoni Carbonara. While the flavor mostly derived from the bacon, the pasta was al dente and chewy, and the savoy cabbage popped with each bite. We also ordered the Ricotta Agnolotti, where the vodka sauce really set the dish apart.

Lastly, the Paloma I ordered was very smoky and bitter - a bit more than I was expecting! Overall, it was a great dining experience, even despite it being a noisy evening due to what seemed to be a birthday party near our table, and some long stretches without service.

Came here for brunch. Breakfast sandwich was very much overpriced for what it was, but the scrambled egg crostino was delicious, and the latte was decent as well. Nothing special about the pancakes (servers must've thought so too, because they forgot this order for over half an hour and we had to remind them twice). Good for large groups.

I've been here many times and have enjoyed myself every time... except this Sunday. Whether or not any online reader feels inclined to believe a stranger's story is up to them entirely. I am posting this review as a warning to other diners based on the belief that it is one that I would want for myself. 

Our bill was about $320, and we returned the check with four fifty dollar bills and eight twenty dollar bills, all of the cash clipped together. Our meal was good (albeit we waited an hour and thirty minutes for our entrees in what was, at 5PM, an essentially empty restaurant). Our service was good, too. I am not here to tear Bar Primi to shreds (mostly because it simply doesn't deserve it), but I do want to express my regretted disappointment in not only what occurred on Sunday night, but with the way the situation was handled by their manager, Justin, who may want to consider looking for a career in another industry, perhaps one where customer retention isn't a necessary skill set. 

My aunt (a CPA for thirty years, if that matters any) counted our bill thrice. She had  brought four fifty dollar bills in her wallet and knew without an inkling of a doubt that all of them had been placed securely inside the check presenter. While I went to bring our car around, my family was approached by our server and told we underpaid while they were waiting outside on the sidewalk. There were only two fifty dollar bills in the check presenter, he said. Not wanting to make a scene in front of the group, my aunt paid the "remainder" of the bill on her credit card and ceased her protesting after realizing the futility of her word. 

I was quite upset to learn our server approached my aunt when the rest of my family and I knew the cash we provided was not only sufficient, but generous. The service was good, and we wanted to tip a bit more than 20%, so we did. This was something we discussed at the table as we laid out the cash. There was no money under the table or on the seats, and each of the members of my party checked their wallets to ensure the mistake was not on their part. If it were, they would have profusely apologized and handled the oversight accordingly. Bar Primi, so it turns out, does not offer its patrons this same courtesy. 

I tried calling the restaurant, but as Primi diners may know, there is literally no phone number to reach them at whatsoever. I texted the customer service number and asked that they call me, and got on the phone with Justin this morning who, if nothing else, was prompt in getting back to me.

Justin's stance was that it was a commonplace occurrence for customers to miscount their cash and that this is what may well have occurred. I explained to him that each of us had only had one glass of wine at the beginning of our meal and that if there was any chance we may have miscounted, there must be an equally plausible chance that his staff could have been mistaken, too. Justin was not prepared to admit this possibility as readily as I had hoped, but I moved on.

By this point, I was hoping we could move on to how we might amend the situation, but I quickly realized that Justin wasn't really trying to fix anything, including our takeaway from the experience. I've worked in restaurants for almost decade, but it doesn't take this kind of experience to know that when an inconsistency occurs in customer service, management should do what it can to ameliorate its conceivable error in order to keep its patrons coming back. In my case, I was met with ambivalence and coolly given little more than what has been explained above. 

I cannot think of any way to provide further evidence of my claim, and admit that, as a long time Yelp user myself, I might be weary to trust the words of a random user if the roles were reversed. Still, if you take anything from this review: DO NOT PAY IN CASH AT BAR PRIMI. Go sometimes, for the decent (though nothing special, as other reviewers have noted) fare and the comfortable decorum, but be aware that your patronage may be more disposable than you'd imagined. Personally, I won't be returning through those doors ever again unless it's to collect the $100 that "mysteriously disappeared" from us.
This is a good pasta spot not to be confused with Bar Priti. It has really good pasta options. The carbonara is excellent and so are the meatballs. The vibe is cool, and they have cool cocktails.

GREAT VIBES & GREAT FOOD -- I came here with my family for dinner and sat in a booth on the second floor, and the best two parts are by far the vibes & food. The atmosphere (especially the booth) was cool and comfortable and the food was excellent (highly recommend the chicken marsala and tiramisu).

Our family had a great time and we'll definitely be back.

We heard they have great tiramisu, so we showed up without a reservation. The host was so nice - gave us a table even though we told him we wanted desserts only. Eventually we ended up ordering a pasta, a spritz and a tiramisu. I don't think the tiramisu was the best but it wasn't bad at all. The pasta (Broccoli pesto) was good but little heavy on the broccoli (obviously). 

Their service was mind blowing and I'll definitely go back for a full experience, because of how genuinely they care.
Had dinner there tonight and had such a great time. Food was delish but more than anything the team was amazing! Just so kind and helpful and welcoming! Can't wait to go back. Thank you!

I am torn between giving this place 3 and 4 stars. The food has always been good but each time we go the service seems to be worse. This time you couldn't get the waiter to come to the table for dear life. His wine recommendations were really bad. This happened last time as well. As a matter of fact the wine list is bad in general. It needs to be refreshed. But the food -- The food is so good! In a nutshell: go for the food but don't expect service to be on par with Locanda Verde and skip the wine and opt for cocktails instead.
food, service, and ambiance was great! the pasta was fresh and really delicious. the whipped ricotta was definitely the standout through for an appetizer. we loved it! would go back again

I've been here twice and it has been great both times. The service is amazing and the ambience is super relaxing and warm, but it's a little pricey. Overall, it's a must-go for anyone that wants amazing Italian food!!!

I ordered the cacio e Peppe and we had the rice balls to share. I also had a froze. The cacio e Peppe was good, not great, and the froze was not good. The rice balls were delicious though! My husband liked his meal, but overall I felt that the food, ambience, and prices make it not worth it to go here.
Blonde female hostess was incredibly rude, ruined the experience from the beginning. Did not want to seat us despite having reservations acted like it was personal, unprofessional.

Ordered the Ricotta crostino hazelnuts, truffle honey $11.75 (Pictured is 1/2 of one). It was delicious, a good balance of texture and flavor. However, it's not worth paying $11.75 for one piece. Make the pieces a bit smaller and put two. The bread was stale too so the bite wasn't as enjoyable. Fresh fluffy bread (in the center of the loaf), especially cut so thick is key. The crust could also have been crispier. The condiments made up for it, especially with the little touch of honey and truffle oil, but for the price, I'm surprised by the portion. 

We also ordered the rigatoni alla norma. The pasta was al dente, which is good, unless it's too al dente, which I thought it was. 
Service wasn't great either. The waiter was nice but not very helpful and only came once to check on us. I had to ask for things several times, instead of him taking the initiative. 

Overall, was good food, but a bit pricey and staff could maybe be a bit more energetic and proactive ... good ambiance and hostesses at the front were friendly.

I really wanted to love this place more. The location has two floors and can seat more people than typical restaurants in this area. We dined for friend's birthday dinner. We started with the octopus and the Brussel sprouts. Hands down the best sprout I have ever had. I got the squid pasta and we finished with tiramisu for dessert. The pasta was delicious and very flavorful. It has a slight spice to it so warning for those who don't love too much spice. Ordered a few bottles of wine - the wine selection is stellar. 

I would rate this place 5 stars for the food but we kept being rushed by our waitress through the meal and as soon as we got the checks was asked to leave in 5 minutes so they could seat the next party. We hadn't even been there an hour and a half. Disappointed because we still had some dessert wine to finish and felt very rushed.

This place is great! I ordered the squid ink pasta because I was feeling adventurous, and it turned out to be one of the delicious dishes I've ever had! It's a must try. The service is fast and the drinks are strong. This is an absolute YES for date night in my book. The only problem I had was the seating was so close it felt like I was having dinner with strangers. But if you're sat at the right table, it shouldn't be a problem.

Had an overall very brunch experience here - ambiance was nice (not too loud) food was relatively basic but nothing to complain about, and service was quite good. Pomodoro wasn't all that filling though

Had a great dining experience at Bar Primi. Dined here with a group of 6 and pretty much tried most of the items on the menu. My favorites and thoughts down below.

SQUID INK PASTA: Aaldente and very flavorful. Had a slight kick to it which made this pasta dish unique/delicious. 

Penne Carbonara: I would describe this dies in three words. Rich, creamy, and perfectly seasoned. I appreciated the sizable pieces of bacon and the cabbage was a great addition. 

Brussel Sprouts: Cooked perfectly and topped with Parmesan.  Chefs kiss!

Paloma: If you're a fan of mezcal, this is a must. CHEERS!!

Came here for a brunch catchup with a group of friends. We made a reservation for 11:45am on a Saturday, which I would say was a great time choice because the restaurant (at a great spot in Bowery, with two floors and a lovely ambiance overall) was not at all crowded when we first sat; by the time our brunch was winding down, approaching 1pm, it was packed! So, would recommend an earlier brunch if you want to avoid crowds, particularly on weekends. In terms of the food, we all loved what we got! I had the breakfast pasta, which was scrumptious. If you aren't a kale lover, ask for light kale or have it removed because there definitely is a good portioning of it on the dish. The sauce brought the whole dish together quite nicely. Other dishes at our table included the penne ragu alla bolognese with ricotta, cavatelli with vodka sugo, and the funghi scramble. Everything was thoroughly enjoyed.

The thing keeping this rating from being 5/5 would have to be the service. The hostess was great, and initially the wait staff was good as well. Every one of us noticed, though, that shortly after we sat down it seemed that staff wanted us to move briskly through our meal. It felt odd considering the lack of people in the restaurant, particularly for the first half hour or so. Even once things started picking up, there were still sufficient open tables--not to mention the fact that there were other groups who were either (1) larger than ours, (2) that had been there even before we arrived, or (3) both 1 and 2! Staff hovered near us a lot and after leaving the restaurant we all felt confused as to what it was about our party that had them silently but still clearly eyeing us/pushing us along. Everyone had ordered an entree, plus most of us got drinks, as well. Not the best feeling.

There are riffs on this name all over the city, Bar Pitti, Bar Primi Dona, Bar Peeni, I can't figure it out, but a bit chilled and needing a bathroom desperately, this Bar Primi shouted out at its perch on the Bowery.

The ground floor bar is very charming, and oh so European, something NYC specializes in.  Other American cities can't pull off this European vibe.  Andrea was our welcoming bartender/server, and her warmth enhanced the experience of Bar Primi.  She helped me choose the Penne Ragu Bolognese, which was done Al dente, with the perfect amount of sauce.  It was delicious.  I shall return to Bar Primi, the perfect respite in the East Village.

Went here the other night for dinner. Food was alright, nothing to write home about. I ordered the chicken Marsala and wow was it salty. The rice balls were tasty though. Ambiance is nice and the gelato was honestly some of the best I've ever had. That being said the entrees me and my group ordered just weren't that great.
Pretty tasty food and great service. We got a prefixed menu for large groups, my faves were the ricotta with honey, arugula salad, orecchiete, and penne ragu.

Returned to finally try the squid ink pasta, which not only looks amazing, but has stellar reviews. It's $27.50, which is insanely expensive considering the portion size and amount of crab in it. 

I was quite surprised it was just "meh". The pasta is cooked Al dente, which is great, but the flavor is so so. I didn't find it memorable at all. Would definitely skip next time.
i ordered their Brussel sprouts appetizer, chicken marsala, squid ink pasta, and broccolini. it was all really good and the ambiance is nice. the service was average but not bad.

Satisfy any craving for Italian food - the menu has all of the options you might desire. While prices are on the higher side, the food was fresh and delicious. We ordered the kale insalata, which combined the kale with apples, roasted garlic and walnuts, along with the grilled octopus, that came atop potatoes. A perfect place to sit at the bar, order a glass of wine, and enjoy a meal of good, high quality food.

Worth the hype. We were so pleasantly surprised by the ricotta crostino hazelnuts and it tasted like homemade ricotta. We were a party of 3 so we made sure it came to serve 3. You have to get it.

I was skeptical about the Sicilian tomato rice balls but they everything and more. Another must order. The tomato also isn't too strong so there's a good balance of flavors.

For my main entree, I can see why the squid ink campanelle is so popular. It's a bit spicy (which I love) and cheesy. It's very filling so after a few bites I was full but it made for great leftovers.

My only complaint would be it was extremely loud so you struggled to hear the people at your table. Also, the frose was too sour and so frozen it was hard to drink.

Rude waitstaff. Meals came 20 minutes apart. No apology. Acted like we should be so lucky to be there. Honestly would have given a better review if there was some sort of warmth on the part of the host/manager whoever the short guy was.

In all honesty, I don't really care much for pasta places if there's nothing standing out on the menu and that's how I felt about Bar Primi. While the pasta was good, it wasn't anything spectacular and it definitely wasn't worth the price, given that most of the pasta doesn't come with meat. We came for brunch, so that may be why. But overall, I felt like the food was pretty basic for what it costs. The burrata was nice, but again, nothing amazi

Stopped in for HH with a few girlfriends. Got seated right away at the communal table, even though it was quite busy. The frose is delicious-- great treat for a hot day. We also got the ricotta app, it was delicious! All in all the price wasn't bad either.

This place has TOTALLY redeemed itself! Before going recently, I had only been once before... right before the pandemic... and I remember it being extremely mediocre. However, this time, Bar Primi was absolutely phenomenal! I started with an espresso martini, which was perfectly balanced, and then I had squid ink pasta as my main. I ate the entire dish and felt perfectly satisfied after finished. The sauce was like and garlicky and I loved how they added peppers to make it a little extra spicy. Although the dishes are a bit pricey, you can still find yourself spending less than $50 if you get a drink and an entree. The only downside to this place is the service. The servers are slow and are not extremely attentive.

Pretty cool location in the East Village - not too packed on a Sunday evening, but had enough people to make it comfortable. Service was a bit slow, but food was definitely worth it! The tomato rice ball appetizers were so good - the star was the basil pesto at its base, we couldn't get enough of it. The ricotta agnolotti was a bit "over-cheesed", but damnit if it wasn't good. Not sure if I'd come back here necessarily given how many similar spots there are, but it was well worth it for one time!

TLDR: A great spot for casual italian fare in an elevated setting. 

We started with the Rice Balls which were paired with a wonderful pesto sauce. The ravioli and the bucatini were both flavorful and not too overwhelming. The cook on the pasta was perfect! 

I only dont give this restaurant a 5 stars because though we had a reservation we werent able to be seated until 30 mins after. I would plan ahead and account for this if you're going during a busy time.

Great service. Good bartender. We were sitting outside, it was cold and they accommodated us with pleasance. 

The food: Exquisite arancini, yummy cheese + honey, delicious pasta made in-house. Good stuff from a homely establishment. Highly recommend. 5/5 from the Inspector.
Salads were excellent - Beet salad and burrata salad were delicious. Decent vegetarian options. No pizza. Service was fine. Pretty expensive. Family friendly.

We stumbled upon this gem a Thursday night after a workout. Let's get straight to the point: the food was nothing short of AMAZING! Our server was great! The wine options were good. If I were able to remove a half star I would only because we purchased a bottle of wine and it came open to the table. It was not opened at the table. I also ate outside in their very warm sitting area. I never stepped inside, I cannot speak for the inside at all. I will definitely return for anytime I want a guaranteed GOOD Italian meal.

I had a fabulous dinner here with my mom and sister last night! We decided to come here before seeing a show at The Public since it was in walking distance. We were 15 minutes late and they were super accommodating.

The service was quick and efficient! I loved the glass of pinot grigio I had. It was full of flavor and had a pink color to it. Very unique!
 
We decided to share the ricotta toast and rice balls for appetizers. Both were FANTASTIC! I loved the ricotta toast with the truffle honey and hazelnuts. All the flavors combined perfectly. The tomato rice balls were awesome and the basil aioli was delish! 

For my entree, I got the linguine. If you love garlic, you have to get this! There was a bit of spice and the breadcrumbs added a nice crunch. I would definitely get this again! 

We decided to share the mocha panna cotta and gelato for dessert. They rotate their gelato flavors daily. We went with the peanut butter. OMG were this desserts amazing! They were a nice small portion, so I wasn't too full afterward. 

This is a great spot for a casual, but modern dining experience. It is especially great if you are going to The Public since it is so closeby! I look forward to coming back and trying more of their dishes since everything I tried so far was outstanding.

Every time I come here I'm always underwhelmed.  It's expensive and the pastas are just very very average. In a city with some of the best Italian, they should be doing better. 

Ricotta Crostino: really delicious -- the best thing we got
Carbonara: way too salty, very dry
Pomodoro: very fresh, but plain

Took my mother and sibling on a dinner date for Mother's Day this Sunday . I looked for many places and stumbled upon this one so I wanted to try it. 


The place is really cute ! It has a cozy home feeling to it and it wasn't overwhelming. The pastas we ordered were delicious ( I ordered the fusilli and mom ordered the rigatoni) the bread was fresh and yummy. 

Our server was really busy so we didn't get a lot of attention, which I understood it was busy. But my mom and sibling seemed to enjoy and that was enough for me.

Pretty average and poor service. Also we were placed on a table with a slant and our glasses fell off. we asked to move tables and then they immediately sat another couple at our old table. Guess what, a few mins later their glasses fell off the table too.
Service was really slow, we waited a good 20 mins to even put in drinks orders.
Wouldn't recommend

Came for dinner on a Friday night and was underwhelmed given how hard it was to get a reservation during prime time.

It's affordable for the area, especially the wine. The food and wine were good, we especially enjoyed the arancini. Pastas were good but not amazing. Service was friendly but overstretched and not super attentive. Ambiance was odd, our table was on such a slant glasses fell off and spilled water on the next table. When we asked to move tables, we saw the same thing happen to the next people seated there, seems strange the table wouldn't just be fixed. It was also super loud, hard to carry on a conversation. Overall probably wouldn't return.

The food was robust with thoughtful personal touches on traditional Italian flavors. The chicken piccata was tender, moist, and brightly full of fresh lemon and capers. The brussel sprouts had a perfect char and delighted with their sumptuous seasoning. There was a palpable gasp around our table of ten when guests took a bite of your supple meatballs and bursting tomato sauce. Everyone at the table was overjoyed by the food, the delicious wine selection, the prompt and stately service, and the willingness of the management to allow us to stay beyond our schedule time because we were so happy in every regard. Thank you for creating such a satisfying experience for our guests! Wow! If you are looking to celebrate a special occasion with a large group, Bar Primi is a place you should consider. We were treated so graciously and the service was impeccable.

I cannot understand why this lovely, yummy place only has 3.5 stars. I've been here twice and loved it every time. The pastas are always perfectly cooked and extremely tasty. I've had the pesto pasta and the garlic one and both are excellent. The salads are large, fresh and delicious as well. Atmosphere and service are excellent!

Loved this place on a weekly basis in 2018 and 2019. 
Still enjoyed it during 2020. 
Was looking forward this evening to the beginning of a summer term of gustatory enjoyment when the following incidents took us from surprise to shock and then to indignation.

It started with the arrival of the bottled still water. 
Ostensibly imported Italian water (Oh, stop it. You commit the same Carbon Footprint sin with wine or chocolate or travel or whatever.) 

We learned from living overseas that if the server doesn't bring an unopened bottle of water to the table then you're paying for tap water. 
And that's what the Bar Primi server did. 
Thinking we're just tourists, he had no idea that we know what NYC water tastes like.
Shame, shame, shame!
I shudder to think what they may be doing with wine.

Then came the 'Hey, how come we aren't getting any bread and olive oil this time?'
Sigh.

And after forty minutes, the arrival of an order of spaghetti pomodoro and one of linguini with garlic. 
The pasta on both was cold. Not room temperature, cold.

The spaghetti was palatable only because the sauce had been at a near-boiling temperature.
The linguini had no sauce and no heat. Also, no taste. 
The addition of seventeen shaved membranes of browned garlic does not add taste; it adds a nasty metallic pang. Not flavor.

We would've loved to have mentioned this to a server but for 15 minutes, there were none within hailing distance.
I suspect they knew there was a problem and avoided us in case we decided to give them some hail.

Want to know how to have a good time at Bar Primi?
Come with at least three other people, finish at least two bottles of wine and you'll never notice what's wrong.
You have my blessing and my envy.

P.S. The outside seating is painfully loud. We were so bored from lack of service that both of us downloaded a decibel meter app and discovered that on a Monday evening, it never dipped below 68 and was often in the 80s.

Bar Primi is always a hit -- it's great for a lively, fun, energetic atmosphere and amazing food! It can get a bit loud at times, so make sure to request a quieter table if that's something that bothers you.

The ricotta agnolotti was impeccable: Al Dente fresh pasta, sweet vodka sauce and stopped with light, creamy ricotta. The squid ink campanelle was so unique and delicious (I'd definitely get this again!): packed with spice, fresh crab, and a light, garlicky cream sauce.

My mouth is watering thinking about it!

I've been here four times and each time I've enjoyed myself. Highly recommend the beets and the squid ink campanelle. Beautiful upstairs interior. Service could be a bit quicker - they seemed to forget about us after we were done eating and we had to flag a waiter down. However, the food is delicious and reasonably priced and the space is wonderful. Recommend if you're in the area.

Yum! Such great food and drinks. Loved my mojito. Loved the Brussels sprouts and the squid ink pasta. Garlicy creamy - could've used a bit more crab though. was very dark inside but still a fun atmosphere. Pasta tastes fresh and yummy.

First time at Bar Primi. A friend of mine told me they had the best Frosé and she did not lie! The frose was so good and wasn't two sweet compared to others I've had in the past. For my entree I wanted to try something different and ordered the Bucatini which had lamb crumbles and it was absolutely delicious. I was nervous the lamb would be too much but it was the perfect amount of lamb and noodles. They have a cute outdoor seating which I sat and they offer indoor as well but the inside felt too stuffy.

Had reservations and was seated quickly.  Waited a bit for food but since we had steak, it was understandable.  My steak was tasty and potatoes were crispy, which was perfect.  Food was good, service was decent but it felt stuffy inside and drinks were just ok.  Good enough, just not perfect.
Amazing food- so delicious, cute place with friends, fun environment!!! 100% RECOMMEND!!! The staff is so nice and positive love it here!!!
Came here for brunch with some friends, and it was pretty decent. We tried a variety of pasta, and the favorite was the rigatoni. Prices are expensive but the restaurant and surrounding area is nice.

Their food and ambience are really great. The restaurant is also located in a good area, and with a simple reservation, we didn't have to wait a single minute to get seated. However, the service was a bit slow and we waited for a bit too long to get our main dishes (which were very good).

Excellent service and food today. We loved the Penne and the linguine. Great wine recommendation from the server, a smooth Italian red wine. The man bussing the tables was so prompt and attentive filling glasses and clearing plates without being obtrusive. Did I mention the music?  Wish they would share the Spotify playlist they use.  Great vibe and food. Yes pricy and worth it to treat yourself.
Got the carbonara and it was so divine. Tried my friends carciofo pasta and it was just ok. Ricotta toast and fried zucchini apps were also solid
Still dreaming about the pesto fusilli even days later. Highly recommend getting a few different pastas and split so you can try a bunch without being too full after

5 stars for beyond delicious food. The ambiance is loud and dark, perhaps better for groups than a date. Service was sparse as they were super busy and no bread basket but I'm willing to give it all a pass for the food. 

I opted to share the prosciutto appetizer rather than burrata, and I'm so glad I did. The meat was so soft and supple, leagues above typical cured meats. 

For anyone who loves a hawt tomato based sauce, the bucatini with lamb is a perfect choice. First time I got a pho sized portion for pasta too.

Try it try it try it!

This is a cozy little neighborhood Italian bar and restaurant. The food was good, but not amazing. The service was friendly and helpful. I really enjoyed the ambiance and vibe of the space. I recommend it for a casual dinner or lunch. It would be great for a group.

The service, ambiance and pasta were all incredible. I was impressed with how delicious the pasta was. They also had a good selection of wine bottles. The tiramisu dessert was ok but nothing to rave about compared to the pastas. The crostini app was also very good. I would come back here again.

Delicious brunch! Went for brunch and brought my dog on the sidewalk patio. They brought the dog water and were so dog-friendly and attentive to us humans! Delicious food: the fried zucchini and ricotta toast were great appetizers in particular.

Doesn't look like much to be honest. The inside was mad cute and the bathroom too. The outdoor seating was kinda sus but it's New York so can't really complain. The place was pretty quiet and there were dogs everywhere and they were so cute!! Server was super nice and offered so much help. Everything was pretty standard pricing and we spent like 135 total including tip. We got the Frozé which was nice on a hot day. The penne was delicious and the linguine was pretty standard (we came here cuz they said it was good online.) The tiramisu was so good!! Highly recommend the tiramisu, frozé and the penne!! Btw we came for brunch/lunch so it was pretty quiet.
Tip: sit inside NY bugs are not it!
The stuffed meatball appetizers were delicious and ample. The arugula salad was fresh and delicious the pasta Bolognese it was fantastic. Service was very attentive. Overall great experience.

Went here for an anniversary dinner and had a great time! The waiters were extremely friendly and they even gave us gelato to celebrate the night. The squid ink pasta was amazing and wasn't overly "ocean-y". Make sure to also get the Arancini - we really enjoyed those. Only criticism was that the orecchiette was a little salty~

I went for a group dinner (6 people) and was not disappointed. I would say that the restaurant gives a more quiet, secluded vibe between tables, even though it was busy. We sat on the second floor, and it was pretty hard to see the menu with the dim lighting, so I would suggest having your phone flash light ready. The pastas are definitely better than the steak (I tried 5 different pasta types, with my favorite being the penne). Waiter was very friendly and had fabulous manners. The booth couches were pretty comfy as well.

Very tasty pasta dishes and I liked our experience. 
I really enjoyed the fiori di carciofi but it was just a bit salty (probably from the prosciutto and the percorino together). But, it was salty and I still ate it bc it was very good and I liked that it was different from other things in the menu. The bolognese was good but only complaint was the saltiness from the fusilli with pesto. Way way too much salt there. Service was fine, will come back.

First and foremost I love a place that is easy to make a reservation at. I booked ahead for a group of 6 and it wasn't insane to try to grab a table so great start. 

The food is consistently good across the board. We got a mix of appetizers (broccolini, meatballs, prosciutto) that came out first, and then a round of pastas that were all great (ricotta agnolotti, fusilli, penne, squid ink campanelle). I was pleasantly surprised with everything that it was all good and we took leftovers because we didn't want to waste the fresh pasta! For dessert we got tiramisu that was not noteworthy whatsoever, but not bad. 

Overall cute vibey place with an upstairs seating which is nice and they decorated for fall which was fun. Good pasta, not amazing phenom never heard of flavors, but simple classics done well. It is SO loud though that it's hard to hear, fun for the energy but hard to have a full conversation without yelling.

Given the trendy hard to get into restaurants in the area, it may be enticing to just go here since they are generally open with tables inside and out, but would recommend just waiting it out elsewhere. My date and I split 1 app, 1 pasta and a bottle and it ended up costing way more than at other places where I had my own main. Almost $200 for that is quite crazy. The waiter also popped in to check if we needed anything every 10 min, which at first we thought was attentive, but then came off as a bit aggressive to get us to leave as it was near closing. Overall just an average experience as the fried rice balls were bland and the lamb in the bucatini pasta was soo hard.

My husband and I went to Bar Primi for my birthday this past week. As I've heard, the dining room was noisy and it was a little challenging to have a conversation. I imagine it would be worse on a weekend. We ordered two apps and two pastas. 

-Stuffed meatballs (3/5): four meatballs (not sure what they were stuffed with) in sugo, a super yummy way to make a tomato sauce. They were good but I wasn't wow'd
-Whipped ricotta with honey, rosemary and hazelnuts (5/5): delicious! I usually don't love rosemary as it's too overpowering but it was just right. The honey drizzle was *chefs kiss*
-Spaghetti with clams (5/5): I super loved this dish. The clams were cooked well, no sand. The sauce was delicious and not too salty. I ate it all. 
-Lamb bucatini (4/5): another yummy pasta dish, I enjoyed the texture of the bucatini. It was a tad salty. 

Service was fine overall. Nothing too special and nothing to complain about except our table was super close to the waitstaff so we had to listen to them talk about other tables. 

We would come again if we're in the neighborhood and craving pasta!

Before attending a show at Webster Hall we were searching for a simple place to dine in the east village. Bar Primi was the perfect call. We had a reservation at this Bowery corner hot spot. Our party of four were  cordially greeted and were seated Al fresco. Our server expedited our requests for cocktails and a great bottle of Italian wine. Appetizers of Burata and Parma ham was delicious. Risotto balls with basil pesto was equally prepared. However the highlight app was an heirloom tomato salad. Of course for entrees it was the house made fresh pastas. Bow ties tossed in olive oil garlic and broccoli rapini was just like grand ma used to make. The angoletti (half moon ravioli) with creamy ricotta filling was four star. Rigatoni in a tomato and meat ragout was on the mark. This little gem on the Bowery corner is not to be missed when in the downtown village. Bravo to the most professional staff I have experienced in quite some time.

Love this place!
Celebrated bday dinner with aunt. Pasta was light, delicious and addictive. Beet salad hit all the notes. 

Shoutout to Matt P!

So I have to say, in general
I love the atmosphere of this place. The food was exceptionally good. I had two issues with this place. first off, there was an extremely large table set next to us pretty much taking us the only other tables in the restaurant. It was full of 20 women who apparently had some business success that happened today. They were taking turns one at a time, standing up and speaking and cackling, and making these loud Woohoo yada yada Woop sounds screaming every single time someone talked. I'm sorry but I'm very happy for whatever happened with their business but they should've reserved a private room to do this. It was extremely loud and obnoxious to the point that my friend and I could not even hear each other speak. We dropped over $300 on a dinner for two people and had the worst physical emotional experience due to this disrespectful consideration of other people in the restaurant. You do not have events like this unless you have fully rented a restaurant out or a private room. You do not do this when there is another table sitting next to you were you were obnoxiously ruining their conversation. We were not at a Taco Bell we were at a very expensive restaurant that we have been saving up to enjoy for a very long time and that was our experience. When I presented this to the manager when he actually asked me how our night was, all he said was come back and next time it will be a better experience. What manager does not offer some kind of compensation for the current meal, or at the very least an offer of some thing for a next meal. I was extremely disappointed in the management and the attitude. I will say our waitress was wonderful I think she felt bad and overfilled our wine glasses a tiny bit to make us feel better. However, we also ordered an item that never showed up and by the end of the meal it finally showed up which should've been comped. I have been in hospitality for almost 30 years and things like this are unacceptable especially with a place as nice and as well renowned as this place is. I was quite disappointed with the overall experience. I won't be back.  Three stars for the food -2 stars for the disrespectful and unappreciated atmosphere.

My wife and I have been dining at bar Primi since 2018. The food, ambiance, service, staff & management are all AMAZING! We always feel right at home! We have never had a bad experience and this is always our go to for our special occasions. With food this yummy they definitely get busy so I do suggest you make a reservation. We recommend this place 1000%.

I walked into Bar Primi on a casual Tuesday afternoon, was the only one in the restaurant at this point. I sat at the bar and ordered the arancini and agnolotti. The arancini was okay nothing great. It was missing something to give it that extra flavor and bring out everything. The agnolotti was cooked well, if I was being really picky I'd say the agnolotti was really big. In my experience usually they're about bite size pieces, you could definitely cut these and you'd be fine. 

I wanted the agnolotti to be more flavorful as well. The sauce was more of the star rather than the pasta itself. Maybe that is what they were going for. I think overall my experience was good I was just expecting something a little more.

I was pleasantly surprised by this place. Went with a party of six and split a lot of the pastas. I'm not really a pesto person but their pesto pasta really stood out. Their meatball appetizer was also amazing. Great if you want a goof standard pasta. 

As for ambiance, we were away from a lot of people but there were a lot of younger people with large groups of friends, probably eating there before going out. Lots of people with espresso martinis.

I came here with some locals for a girls' dinner. The service was fine (very Italian- they didn't want to answer lots of questions and were impossible to find to pay the check- so very accurate honestly). We ordered lots of dishes to split and they were all quite good. The best part of the meal was the after dinner bitter cocktails as a palate cleanser. I hadn't seen that since being in Italy.

Great food, homemade pastas and dishes.  Good
cocktails.  Staff was very friendly and attentive.  I would go back and recommend to anyone looking for good Italian in the neighborhood that isn't looking for a tradition red sauce kind of place.

Ambiance: Perfect for a date night -- young and trendy vibes and an overall boisterous atmosphere.

Service: On point -- quick with everything, from drinks to food to the check, and polite throughout.

Food: Outstanding -- met my dietary restrictions with gluten free pasta, and both the pasta and ravioli were excellent, on top of a lovely broccolini appetizer.

Fully deserving of five stars and a place I would recommend to anyone looking for high quality italian cuisine.

Had a really nice dinner here last night. The ambience is beautiful and lively, the food was seriously amazing and the service was great. Pretty pricy but the quality of food makes up for it. Our drinks we're great but I will say that seeing my espresso martini was $21 when the bill came was quite shocking considering the other cocktail I had was $14. I almost always order an  espresso martini when I go for a dinner and have never paid such a steep price. Besides that it was wonderful.

Who wouldn't love this spot?! The food is fantastic and the service is attentive and very nice. I highly recommend the Burrata appetizer and the Penne Bolognese with ricotta - delish!! The ambiance is great too, especially during the holiday season. It is a little pricey, but it is a great spot! Worth it.
It's very basic, most of the foods I saw on yelp were not on the menu. The bar tender makes great cocktails

The Staff at Bar Primi is top notch, and I must say RUN don't walk to this establishment. As a first timer to this restaurant while also planning my company's holiday dinner here I felt very overwhelmed with the amount of planning that went into coordinating this. However, Justin & Jackie whom I was in constant contact with to the point of annoyance (haha), handled me with such ease and patience and professionalism and assured me everything would be perfect. I can happily say we were treated like queens and kings at our dinner, and the servers and staff were so amazingly professional, kind, organized, and patient with such a large group like ours. The beautiful decor and trendy hip energy is totally as the kids would call it "A Vibe" and I loved it. I had a few cocktails before my dinner, and they were excellently crafted this is the type of place I would also come for just a cocktail too if I wasn't looking to eat and just wanted to hangout at the bar as well. The food was AMAZING I don't think I've had a better prepared steak in NYC and we did a sampling of all their appetizers and everything was delicious. All our staff loved their entrees and no one's plate was left empty. For dessert I think I had a whole tiramisu for myself and gelato and I felt transported back to Italy again. I could rave more and more about how much of a gem this place is, but you'll just have to experience it yourself!

Went here for my birthday! And staff were so friendly and welcoming!  Ordered appetizers stuffed meat balls, Brussels sprouts, and the antipasti salad.  For primi, I ordered the squid ink pasta. It was good, but it needed more garlic cream. And for second I. We ordered the Chicken piccata which has a perfect amount of sauce. And the branzino, which was a bit too oily, but it's still pretty good.. the drinks were amazing too. And the ambiance is so cute and intimate great for date nights and girls night out! Overall a great restaurant!

the location and ambience is great inside the restaurant. it's very cute, nice lighting and decoration inside. the staff and service is amazing. everyone is friendly. our food came very quickly after we ordered and it all tasted amazing. i would highly recommend.

I went for dinner during Restaurant Week and had an ok meal -- solid but not noteworthy or worth an additional visit. There are plenty of Italian spots in NYC, and while nothing stood out, all the food was very classic. I had the arancini, chicken parm, and tiramisu. What did surprise me was that the portions were so big for personal plates (and for RW even). I enjoyed the Lambrusco and gin cocktail too.

Overall the ambiance is cute and it's a casual spot.

This might be the easiest 5 star review I have ever left... everything we ordered was incredible. Started with the arancini and the fresh mozzarella with prosciutto which were both incredible. For the main entrees we ordered the fusilli with pesto, the ricotta angliotti, and they were able to modify that to make a gluten free version with penne as well! The service was outstanding and the food was incredible. Definitely coming back to this spot!
I've been wanting to try this place for a while now & it didn't disappoint. Apps were good portions & drinks are made well. Pesto pasta was buttery & delicious. Service was great too!

My fiancé and I went here to celebrate our anniversary during New York's restaurant week, everything was amazing!! The service was absolutely exceptional. Our waiter was extremely attentive.
