The food was top tier! Our favorite from the restaurant week menu was the Spaghetti, best pesto pasta hands down. If you're looking for great Italian restaurant, this is our new favorite go-to, in Lower Manhattan this is it! We can't wait to come back & visit.

OVER RATED PASTA . Not the best pasta you can get ! Prices are ridiculous and drinks arnt even that great . Service isn't that bad but they should get better servers on the floor who knows what they're doing . Wouldn't recommend at all.

Bar Primi had decent Italian food for a good price but it definitely wasn't the best I've had. 

We got their Sicilian Tomato Rice Balls for an appetizer. It was crunchy on outside but a little too mushy on inside for my liking. The rice ball itself could have had more flavor but the pesto underneath it was flavorful!

The Cavatelli in vodka sauce was pretty good. The pasta itself was cooked just right, but the sauce itself had more tomato flavor than creaminess. It made me question if vodka sauce is just better suited for pizza:)

The Cacio e Pepe was buttery with a hint of cracked black pepper. It was great if you're into subtle, not really a burst of flavor!
Ambiance was great. Server was very helpful. Drinks were refreshing. My pappardelle pasta was the absolute best.

Love this place and have loved it for quite some time. Just a great crowd pleaser with a fun atmosphere for a night out on a date, with friends or family. The bolognese is my favorite with the cold cheese on top and I don't think I'm alone. Not going to absolutely blow you away with food but everything is very good and the prices are mid level.
Not bad, not good. A very average experience all around. Brussels sprout app was ok, pasta was fine, service was meh. Just a very unremarkable experience.

Another great italian spot. Can you find the same exact menu at any other italian spot in the city? Yep. Can you get the same vibes at most other italian joints? Yep pretty much. Nothing is remotely or inherently "special." It ticks all the boxes you would expect it to. Does that mean skip on it? No way! It is quality food, wine, service, prices, and vibes. Im just saying theres a million other places exactly like it. Will i be going back? Not running, but sure!
The server was super nice and all the hosts were really accommodating. The music was low and nice .the food was good. I recommended the ricotta crostini and the sicilian tomato rice ball

I would actually rate Bar Primi a 3.5. I thought the food was good, but the overall experience ok. It was a Friday night and the restaurant was quite busy and the service reflected that. The restaurant can be quite loud when full and you should be prepared for that. 

I started with a Lucky 13 cocktail - bourbon, cynar, heimat ny cranberry, and walnut bitters. It was good, but nothing really stood out about the cocktail.

For an piccolini I had the Ricotta Crostino topped with hazelnuts and truffle honey. The ricotta was nicely whipped and they certainly didn't skimp on the hazelnuts. It had the right amount of honey, truffle and rosemary. It all worked together and was very good. 

For my second piatti I had the Grilled Branzino with Olive Muffaletta. The fish was moist and grilled well. I thought the Olive Muffuletta would be over-powering, but it worked well with the fish. 

Ordering wine was a bit of a challenge at first, but the server recognized that he was out of his league and got someone to help me. I had a bottle of 2021 Occhipinti FRAPPATO/NERO D'AVOLA 'SP68', Sicily and enjoyed it.

I am glad I tried Bar Primi, but not sure if I'd go back again. Nothing was bad or horrible, just not fabulous enough for me to want to go back again.
good Italian restaurant with decently sized plates
Loved the food and the ambience. It was cozy, yet enough space so it was not too loud.

Overall an OK spot. Solid Italian food for the price but you can find better. Pasta was a bit salty. Drinks were fine. Good clientele. Surprisingly tough to get a reservation at sometimes. Good location to eat at for a late reservation before going out in East Village or Lower East Side

Bar primi has potential, they have outdoor seating which is great right now and makes it easy if you have a dog. The food is good, but my rating applies to the lack of care they take with regard to allergies. I told the server I have an allergy and he may melt have understood what it was, so he should have asked more questions. 

Instead, several items contained the allergen and when I pointed this out on the first item he blamed it on the kitchen, for the second item another server told me it was not in the dish. I was having a reaction so I knew the allergen was in the dish, and it is  gaslighting to tell someone an allergen is not in the dish while they know it is. Another server confirmed it indeed was included and had another one made without it. 

I encourage Bar Primi to train your staff to handle allergies with more care. I'm still dealing with the fallout of the reaction 5 days later.
Favorite spot in NYC! Not overpriced. The linguini and clams is delicious but can be a touch too spicy
Enjoyed my drink and my squid pasta! Would come back just for that. The service was good and the ambiance was great for a dinner. Had a great time, would recommend.

After being turned away from Il Buco on a Monday night (what is this city coming to???) we headed right over to Bar Primi.  Pre-Covid, when we lived on the East side, their squid ink pasta with crab was a Friday night take-in favorite.  Would it hold up, or had it gone downhill?  It was delicious - a bowl of comfort, along with the orecchiette with broccoli rabe and sausage.  Meatballs were good, if a little salty.  The burrata with roasted peppers was excellent - doused in olive oil and smeared on good crispy bread.  Is this pasta the light and delicate variety?  No.  Is this authentic Italian food?  No.  It's not trying to be.  

Service was attentive and friendly, until a large table celebrating a birthday landed our server in the weeds.  Ambience was decent (somehow, there is always an ambulance parked outside the glass windows, lights spinning), but I seem to remember it being very loud on the weekends.

Bar Primi is always a great choice, and this time in particular they went above and beyond. The host was very communicative and attentive to fulfilling a special request and made sure it happened, even on a busy Saturday night, which we really appreciated (didn't catch their name, unfortunately). 10/10 always, and we'll keep coming here to celebrate every time. Thanks!

Our hostess ,Izzy, greeted us warmly , made us feel welcome and appreciated. 
The wait staff was attentive and friendly.
The food was outstanding!
thank you for a wonderful evening!
I love the pasta and drinks from here and the ambiance is very lovely. The service here is great as well even when it's super busy.

Great spot to take folks looking for a good Italian meal. Very accommodating to my dairy allergy. Great wine list. Well spaced out and overall great ambiance.  I had pasta with sausage and broccoli, and a ton of bread.  Large portions.

Terrible service.  All over you to place your order then nobody.
Way too long for drinks to arrive and the half hour gap between apps and mains was ridiculous.

Mains came - asked for another round of drinks with the mains and parm 

Half done with mains going cold before drinks arrived


Finished the mains before the parm arrived

$90 a person 

Not worth it

good spot for solid pasta and other dishes!

came here on a weeknight for a dinner - we made a reservation but there was a good amount of seating open. cute outdoor seating space and a bar as well

appetizers - 
beet salad (3.5/5): flavorful dish that's great for anyone who loves beets. served with pistachios and a yogurt sauce
ricotta crostino (4.5/5): probably one of the most popular dishes here - the ricotta is amazing and the honey glaze adds good flavor as well. hazelnuts on top as well, overall this was probably one of the top things i tried!

pastas - 
squid ink campanelle (4.5/5): loved this one the most out of the three pastas we tried, has shredded crab and is slightly spicy. 
fusilli (3.5/5): very green - a pesto sauce and broccoli that kind of gets hidden in all the sauce lol. solid pesto pasta, nothing super special!
bucatini (3.5/5): lamb pieces plus red sauce. solid pasta but nothing special about the flavor. 

the pastas were all great, the flavor was solid but all of them were al dente and perfectly cooked!

dessert - 
tiramisu (4/5): shared a tiramisu with the table, the portion is quite large but it was very solid - one of the better tiramisus i've had

overall, service was good and the atmosphere is nice to meet up with friends or grab a drink. would definitely recommend!
Alfonso and staff were amazing, food and wine was delicious.  The restaurant ambiance was private, an amazing experience.
The food is AMAZING. We were happy with every plate. Lovely atmosphere. Recommend trying the sides too!
Great! Wonderful food and ambience, will definitely be back very soon. Had a fun time.
The ambiance, food, and service were on point! I really enjoyed my meal, my friends did as well. I highly recommend coming to this place; I will be going back for more delicious food and drinks.

Outstanding service (our water glasses were never empty) cute atmosphere( a soft industrial with a touch of farmhouse?), spotless ( have never seen cleaner bathrooms in a restaurant and decent food. We visited on a Saturday , arriving around 11:30 AM and the restaurant was fairly empty. We did notice walk-ins were seated and attended to rather quickly throughout our stay. Food was tasty, although there was not much of a variety. They gave us a brunch menu, so perhaps there is more variety at dinner. We did have someone with a variety of digestive challenges and she was only able to eat some yogurt with fruit. Their meatballs were OK, their vodka sauce was good, and their pasta was good as well. Give it a try!

Went down there to celebrate my friends 25th  We got to our reservation 10 mins early but big woop. We were seated at exactly at our reserved time. The staff was nice and friendly and our waiter specifically was attentive. The location is also very cute and the ambiance is wonderful but thought the lights were a bit too dim. Felt a bit blind in there. We were seated upstairs for the night. A bit loud in the restaurant bc my friend and I were yelling a bit to be heard  but let's talk FOOD. I'm a vegetarian and I got the fusilli with pesto and I felt I was chewin on some grass. The flavors must be playing hide and seek with me bc they was no where to be found...Only hint of spice in there was the salty broccoli. The food was so bland it negated the entire exp ‍ the rice ball item I got wasn't so bad but again... main entree was sad
Fresh pasta in a good group eating environment in the east village, little pricey for the menu but overall a solid go to place

Sat at bar on a busy Friday night. Bartender was on it even though she was slammed. She made great recommendations. The food was so satisfying and top notch. Great food, great wine, fun hip ambient vibe. 
Deciding between this place and another? Just come here it's the best!
The food and service were both great! We got sat immediately and our food came out quick. This place had a wonderful ambiance!

The fact this place has so many sorta decent reviews blows my mind. I would put it in the category of one of the worst meals I have ever had in New York City. I went with 3 people and not one person liked anything. The cocktails were terrible (worst frose -- avoid.) the rice balls were terrible (mushy / soggy / gross). The pastas (linguine, bucatini, and fettuccine) were terrible. No one finished anything. We took a few bites, grabbed the check, and ran out to go to another restaurant. What a terrible place .

The vibe inside is bustling, usually busy, and can feel somewhat small so be prepared for noise level. The ambience is dark, service is friendly, and food is good overall. To start, I would definitely recommend the ricotta crostini with hazelnuts and truffle honey. The ricotta is whipped just right and the hazelnuts add a unique crunch with sweet coming in from the honey. Truly delicious! The kale salad was forgettable. I love that their pastas are made fresh with non-gmo flour and organic eggs. You can taste the freshness of the pasta and the high quality ingredients. They have a good selection of Italian wines that pair nicely as well as signature cocktails.
I wasn't super impressed with their restaurant week menu nor the quality of the food.  It was good, but nothing out of the ordinary.  The salad and white wine were great.

A vegetarian review! 

Came here for a late Saturday lunch. Was not hard to get a reservation. 

The apps are much better than the mains. We got the crostino and the burrata. Both were good. The fettucini tasted a lot like sweet corn soup and the fusilli was low on salt (tasted much better after adding some salt!)

Service was very good! Music inside was a little loud but manageable.

Just recently tried this place for the first time with 3 friends. For appetizers we shared the meatballs and rice balls. Both were smaller than expected, about the size of golf balls. For me they were both just ok. Nothing great or memorable. 
We all ordered pasta dishes for our main course. I ordered the spaghetti with clams ($29) but was able to switch the pasta to linguine. The dish was served in a large bowl but was maybe only half full. There was maybe a dozen or so clams but they were the smallest clams I've ever seen. In my opinion it lacked flavor and the portion size was on the small side. 
On the plus side the servers and staff were helpful and attentive and the restaurant itself had a nice atmosphere. In total we had 2 appetizers, 4 pasta dishes, 3 beers and 1 cappuccino. We each paid $60 including tip. For the amount of food we received and the quality of the food it wasn't worth it. I ended up buying food somewhere to satisfy my hunger. Doubtful I will go back.
We got the ricotta toast, the bucatini amatriciana, and the penne bolognese. All three were very good, the service was good even though the restaurant was packed. Would come back again!

The appetizers blew me away!! The ricotta toast with honey and hazel nuts was amazing and the prosciutto and mozzarella MELTED in my mouth. I also really loved the broccoli pesto it was super creamy and not too filling. The bolognese was also super yummy. 

My friend got the lamb bucatini and that is the one thing I was iffy about, but other than that the vibes were really cool and great food!

Outstanding Italian pasta and sauces . We had the fresh made cavatelli, the breakfast spaghetti (carbonara) and the penne .
.Started with the stuffed meatballs .Perfect size and tender .. Loved the ambiance so much ordered all the desserts , including pistachio gelato and strawberry zabaglione. Good cocktails and Italian soda for libations .

Get the ricotta crostino! Trust me, you will not regret it. It was amazing and not something you would find anywhere else.  

I was not expecting the food to be great here after reading the reviews but the squid ink pasta was pretty decent. Not the best I've had but it was good and the portion was generous! Maybe the restaurant  saw the bad reviews about the tiny portion and changed it?  Anyway, I would come back here to try the rest of the menu and and also just for that ricotta. 

The service though was shockingly horrible. The service was slooooow and our waiter was so nonchalant and inattentive, it was very frustrating. Like hello what am I tipping you for?!?? That kinda ruined it a bit for me, but the vibe here was great on a Friday night.

This cozy-cool gem hit the spot for this American in London who misses Italian-American food something awful!

A local-based friend made the reservation when i told her I really just needed some meatballs already and she nailed it. 

I arrived on a stormy summer night, and waited at the bar with a delicious No-groni that I highly recommend. Not too sweet or bitter and a proper drink that won't feel like you're missing out. The atmosphere and chill, jazzy/mellow music was the perfect antidote to a frenetic subway ride from midtown to beat the rain. 

We sat upstairs which was a great spot to watch the rain that eventually blew through, and ordered a couple small plates and shared main. It was the perfect amount of food for two - we left satisfied but not overfill and got to try a few things. 

I will say the entrée was small for the price and just not a crowd pleaser (the fettuccine with cream sauce and corn). But we enjoyed everything else from ambiance to service to small plates. 

Total bill was $94 which included two drinks (both mocktails), zuchhinni frites, stuffed meatballs and fettuccine).

Made a reservation for a Friday night and had a solid meal here. They were sadly not serving Frosé (they invented it here!) so I got the Capri cocktail instead. Also tried the Vesuvio cocktail. My boyfriend and I shared:

+ Insalata greca
+ Stuffed meatballs 
+ Squid ink campanelle
+ Fiori di carciofi
+ Tiramisu

The tiramisu was by far the best thing, and the meatballs were also particularly delicious.

I think AC's newer spot Carne Mare at Pier 17 is better, but this holds up!

Absolutely LOVED the food here. The ambience is amazing, perfect for a date night or a group of friends too. 
For apps we got the ricotta crostino and I'd 10/10 recommend it. 
For mains I got the ricotta agnolotti in vodka sauce and it was delicious. Super cheesy and creamy, and def don't miss the tiramisu for dessert! 
Staff is also really polite and great service.

Wow! I recently went to Bar Primi on a celebration trip, and it was out of this world! The food was defiantly the best I had in the city! The atmosphere was so warm and cozy. It had been raining all day so the candlelit space felt perfectly cozy to wind down a cold day. If the atmosphere wasn't warm and cozy enough, the food was decadent and rich and absolutely cozy and delicious! The espresso martini was top notch and the staff made you feel right at home! To round out the experience they even had cute matchbooks at the hostess stand!

I love Bar Primi. My favorites are the stuffed meatballs and the rice balls as an appetizer. Unfortunately, they took the Bolognese off of the menu, which was one of their very best dishes. Why, I have no idea. It's so disappointing. 
They need to bring it back.

We wound up having the white bolognese, which was good, but doesn't hold a candle to the red. 
So pleeeeaaase, if the owners of this great establishment are reading this, pleaaseee bring back the bolognese!

this place was so packed and i can understand why! the food was gorgeous. i got the pesto fusilli, my friend got the squid ink campanelle, and we shared the ricotta crostini. the crostino was delightful, it was perfect. my friend rated the squid ink campanelle as an 8/10. i thought the fusilli was okay, after a few bites it didn't taste like anything. this place feels homey and nice, i enjoyed coming but im not sure if id come back again for pasta, would def come back for the crostino

Love their froze! I usually wouldn't say that but this one actually doesn't taste too sweet and boy does it actually pack a punch!

I'm also a big fan of their cheese crustini. Get it!

This place is definitely hip and has a good ambiance.

We had a great time at bar Primi as a group of 4. The service was slightly slow, though the restaurant was packed so it is understandable. We each picked a different kind of pasta and picked at each other's, and we all loved them all. My personal favorite was the ragu and the orecchiette. The pasta tasted fresh and homemade, and the sauces were perfect, though on the saltier side. We had to run out the door to catch a show so we didn't get to try the desserts, but I would go back to give them a chance

I really liked their ricotta crostino, but unfortunately not much else. 

We had made a reservation for a party of 5 ahead of time and were seated as soon as we arrived. For appetizers, we shared two of the ricotta crostinos (they come with 2 pieces each), and I thought this was a wonderfully balanced dish with the sweetness of the honey and the crunch of the hazelnuts. For entrees, I ordered the orcchiette which came with broccoli rabe and peperoncino. The pasta itself was cooked fine, but the meat was overly salty and there was not much depth to the actual dish. My friends all ordered the fusilli, which I had tried a bite of and thought the dish was actually too overpowering for more than a couple bites. 

The pastas felt reasonably priced, but the serving size was gigantic so I ended up taking home leftovers.

Bar Primi was wonderful. 

First off, the ambience is great. There are two stories, we sat upstairs. It was just a beautiful restaurant. It had a cozy, yet upscale vibe. 

The pasta you could tell was handmade, it was perfectly al dente and so yummy. The salad was also delicious -- the perfect amount of toppings (aka, a lot of toppings!!!)

Our server was also great. As we arrived, he offered us Prosecco for our anniversary and was also happy to make menu recommendations.
Amazing food, great service and nice ambiance. All pasta dishes where great. Definitely will come back.

Went there for a dinner with family.  It is a nondescript place but quite affordable and with a nice pasta selection. 

Apps - the beets which came in a spicy bed of hummus and yoghurt and pistachios. Generous portion very nice beets.  The octopus was on a beans.  Cold.  Refreshing very tasty. The meatballs were great. I am not a huge fan but I tried a small piece and it was delicious 

Entrees were the pastas and the steak. The pomodoro spaghetti was my choice.  Cooked al dente with plenty of sauce and some Parmesan already sprinkled.  Delicious. The squid ink pasta was tasty but lacked sauce and the crab was sparse.  The steak was delicious! Perfectly seasoned dnd cooked. 

I am not a dessert person but the tiramisu and pistachio ice cream were loved. 

Great service.  Attentive and knowledgeable. Nice old NY ambiance. 

I highly recommend this place!

Decided not to eat here because I did not feel safe with the amount of nuts on the menu as someone who is deathly allergic to them. Was then literally chased down the street by the server to pay for carbonated water that was not consumed.
Good Food. Good service. Good Ambiance. Neighborhood is a bit sketchy. The Bowery is not a very safe place once the sun sets.
Loved the food, the ambiance, great service as well. The ricotta agnolotti was my main dish and was delicious!

Our family had a great lunch at Bar Primi. From the ambiance to the food to the service! We came in on a Sunday afternoon with about 10 people and there were 2-3 other tables seated so seating was not an issue at all. 

We started off with the Chickory Salad, Sicilian Tomato Rice Balls, Ricotta Crostino, and Brussels Sprouts (with pepperoni!) to share as an appetizer. For the main dishes, I ordered the Rigatoni Alla Norma and the table shared Ricotta Pancakes and Breakfast Spaghetti. Everything we ordered was delicious and there were definitely many unique ingredient combinations. If I had to pick, my favorites were the Sicilian Tomato Rice Balls, Ricotta Crostino, and the Breakfast Spaghetti!

I thought this place was super yummy and had great vibes. It would have been 5/5 but the service was really slow (not the staff's fault--the owner needs to staff more workers!) and they didn't have matchboxes which I started collecting way before TikTok ruined my hobby!

Ambiance 
We arrived on a Thursday at 5pm with a group reservation for four. When we arrived, the restaurant was fairly empty but within a few minutes it filled up. We were seated upstairs. The restaurant is pretty, snug and comfortable. 
The booth chairs were a little too soft, so at time I felt like I was looking up to my friends from across the table. Otherwise, the restaurant had a healthy buzz of happy customers chatting away. 

Service 
Matt was our server and he was A++. Water was constantly replenished, dishes came out quickly. Service was friendly. We had a lot of coats and didn't know they had a coat closet/check. If we had known we might have asked to put some of our coats away. 

Food 
The food was delicious. Fresh, well made pasta and sauces. The meatballs were delicious. We had the bucatini, parpadelle, orriechiette, and cacio e Pepe. We all enjoyed our main courses. For dessert we had the budino and tiramisu. SO GOOD! 

Cute spot for date night or out and about with friends.

Really good italian food! Nothing extraordinary about the brussel sprouts in my opinion but the pecorino pasta was pretty delicious! Reasonable price for the portions too. Also enjoyed the whipped ricotta toast.

The Italian restaurant offers well-executed dishes with commendable service in a cool atmosphere.

Food: The culinary experience at the Italian restaurant was commendable, with well-executed dishes presented thoughtfully. While the flavors were satisfying, nothing particularly stood out as groundbreaking.

Service: The service was praiseworthy, as the staff provided attentive and accommodating assistance. The hostess, despite a full house, graciously accommodated a last-minute switch to outdoor dining, enhancing the overall positive dining experience.

Atmosphere: The restaurant's atmosphere struck a delightful balance between laid-back and chic. The cool ambiance added to the overall enjoyment of the evening, making it a pleasant place to unwind and savor the Italian culinary delights.

Solid spot for a nice dinner after work.

I had a reservation with a group of coworkers for Tuesday evening and were seated immediately upon arrival. The restaurant has two floors and we were lucky enough to be seated in a cozy corner upstairs. 

Our table split a few appetizers, including the Sicilian Tomato Rice Balls, Beets, Buratta Cremosa, and Grilled Octopus. Every dish was great, though my favorites were the rice balls and the buratta (the bread that came with it was so fluffy!!). For my main, I ordered the popular Squid Ink Campanelle, which was delicious and had a nice kick of spice, though there could have been bigger chunks of crab. Pasta texture was great and the dish wasn't too salty. I also ordered a Fellini - nothing super special but light and refreshing. 

The restaurant was pretty busy when we were there, but the space is large so it was pretty easy to get a reservation for our group of 7.  Would recommend!

Bread and olive oil appetizer was honestly my favorite part of the meal. You just can't go wrong. The carbonara was pretty good when hit but unpalatable when cold. They use plenty of guanciale, but the chunks are too big so whenever you bit into a piece its like eating porky seawater. The sauce was too watery and didn't coat the pasta well, but the pasta itself was al dente and clearly homemade. 6.5/10

Bar Primi is a decent spot for italian fare. I came here for Sunday brunch with friends, and it was easy to get a reservation. It was not too crowded so you may not need a reservation. Service was good and attentive, and the ambience was very nice (bright, clean, spacious) and perfect for a brunch. It felt cozy inside. In terms of the food: 

Ricotta crostino 4/5: very decadent ricotta with a little bit of honey, truffle, and hazelnut on a crunchy piece of bread! This was really delicious and nice to try. Felt rich and light at the same time! 

The sandwich 2/5: this unfortunately wasn't it for me. My main complaint is the sliced beef... it was dry and completely flavorless. The sandwich tries to compensate with a bit of sauce and a decent pepper jam, but I really didn't enjoy the beef. I'm also not that into the brioche-type bun that the sandwich came on. Sandwich is a decent size but definitely disappointing from a flavor profile.

Wow. Just wow. Small group of couples in our early 40s. This place was amazing. Our waitress hosted us amazingly explaining the menu since some of us needed it. This is not bland food for the masses, this is amazing. We had Brussels, arugula salad, the broschut, the squid-ink pasta (spicy and excellent), some outstanding red wine... phenomenal experience!

Made a reservation for a solo dinner when I was in town for work and was seated right away. The host was so sweet and seated my by a window because he said it was the best spot for people watching. I started with the stuffed meatballs and they were SO good. Meat was tender and the sauce was delicious. Highlight of my meal for sure. I got the rigatoni carbonara for my main course which was not one of the pastas the waiter suggested when I asked him. I will say it was good, but something about it had a strange flavor/after taste. The guanciale in the pasta was incredible though. Serves me right for not taking my servers recommendation! Overall, loved the vibe and would be back again for the meatballs.

Another great dinner at Bar Primi. The first time didn't disappoint so I had to come back and bring a friend to experience the great food and service. The experience was great yet again. The grilled octopus, branzino, and spaghetti and clams were amazing!

Came here for a Sunday brunch because I wanted to make a last minute reservation for 5, and this is one of the few places in the LES with solid reviews where that was possible. We were a little late, but they were very understanding and willing to seat us without our whole party being present. Service was excellent, friendly and warm. One server discreetly brought us more napkins when he saw us struggling with keeping our toddler clean. It was a kind gesture, with a smile and no judgment.
The food was solid. The ricotta toast with toasted hazelnuts and truffle honey was delicious. My breakfast pasta was perfect. The chocolate hazelnut budino was a lovely and light dessert, not too sweet.
Prices are fair for the quality and size of the portions.
Note: there is no changing table if you have a kiddo in diapers!

I had the most delicious meal at Primi!! The vibe was casual, hip iykyk. I was so excited to eat here because they are recognized with a Michelin Bib Gourmand! 

For apps, we ordered the Stuffed Meatballs in sugo and Burrata cremosa peperonata with grilled bread. You can never go wrong with some meatball apps in my opinion. These were golden brown on the outside and tender and juicy on the inside. I could've eaten this whole burrata! The inside was so soft and luxurious. 

For my meal, I ordered the Pennette ragu bolognese with ricotta.Oh my god you this pasta was soooo good!!!  There was not one little morsel left on my plate (also because my boyfriend was stealing some as well lol!) 

My boyfriend ordered the Italian benedict with prosciutto on focaccia and tomato hollandaise. While I didn't try it, it looked phenomenal. He loved it!

Visiting NYC, we took out our nephew and his girlfriend and our dearest friend's son and his girlfriend out to dinner. Bar Primi was the perfect choice for a fun group dinner (though I could see coming back next time for a romantic Bar Primi meal with just my honey).  They gave us a great semi-circle booth that enabled all of us to connect.  The food was flavorful and delicious for meat eaters, pescatarians and vegetarians alike.  Don't skip the hazelnut chocolate budino for dessert (trust me on this).  A highlight was our wait staff --Avery. Avery was Perfect: professional, kind, charming, knowledgeable, made helpful wine recommendations, didn't try to upsell, didn't hover, and was always there exactly when we needed him.  He really added to the entire experience.  We will be back, I hope!
Food was excellent, I had the ricotta pancakes. Service was great. I liked the space but it was chilly in there and the chair was a little uncomfortable.
Absolutely amazing fresh pasta and delicious stuffed meatballs! The ambience and community gathering type intimacy makes it a unique and cool dining experience!

I actually first heard about Bar Primi when I overheard someone talking about it on the train, but I looked it up and it seemed yummy, so voilà, here we are. A few friends and I came by for a weekday dinner; we had a reservation, but it was really empty when we got there (6:30pm ish).

The restaurant is a bit bigger than I expected, since there's a second floor, but even though there's a lot of space, our table was pretty small (it was fine since there were only 3 of us, but it's ordinarily meant to seat 4).
Also the seats of the booth we were in were rather uncomfortable for me heh.

Regardless. We ordered the stuffed meatballs to start, which were pretty good. The meat was savoury (although a little too heavy, I think) and the tomato sauce was very yummy (would have gone nicely with e.g. bread but alas, no bread. For the price I did think portion size was a little small (it's 4 medium-ish meatballs).

We ordered three pastas to share:

- rigatoni carbonara: the sauce felt a little one-dimensional and too salty; there wasn't that much of the usual egg/cheese undertone throughout. I did like that the pasta was nicely cooked to the perfect al-dente chewiness, but the overall flavour profile was definitely a bit lacking. The guanciale was very savoury and yummy, definitely the high point of the dish.

- ricotta agnolotti: so, interestingly I learnt that the main difference between agnolotti and ravioli is that agnolotti is made from one piece of folded pasta whereas ravioli is with two separate pieces stuck together. (fun fact of the day.) this dish was fine-ish; I liked the mouthfeel of the ricotta and agnolotti wrapper together, but I felt like the flavours of the ricotta and the vodka sauce were a bit unbalanced (both rather heavy, and not quite in a complementary way)

- orecchiette: I thought it was surprisingly good, although it did get very mixed reviews around the table. The sauce wasn't too heavy while still adding a nice complement to the broccoli rabe and spinach. The sausage was a bit salty for my taste but I think it worked pretty well with this dish in particular. Pasta also very nicely al dente.

And finally we shared a tiramisù for dessert. I am the biggest tiramisù fan, so of course it was delicious, but not spectacularly so (e.g. I think you could get a similarly above-average slice at many places throughout the city).

Overall, I feel like our meal was pretty OK - nothing particularly bad, but also nothing particularly fantastic. Price point was decent (pretty good compared to many Italian restaurants in the city) but still a little on the higher end.

We made a reservation and arrived on time, but were only seated 15 minutes later. We ordered the spaghetti clams, penette, garlic spaghetti and meatballs. The food was mediocre at best, not quite homey but not really Italian fare standard either. There are probably better Italian restaurants out there. It was also really noisy and almost impossible to have any meaningful conversation. The table service was rather okay, however.

Amazing Michelin recommended restaurant. Affordable and the focus is on the primi meal - contrary to other nice italian restaurants where you're expected to order multiple meals. Amazing food, service, and vibes!!

The food was unbelievably great! Our waiter was friendly & attentive. The location was convenient to our son's NYU apartment. It definitely had the NY bar/restaurant vibe. Indoor & outdoor seating too!

I walk up to a small brick building on a busy corner in Manhattan and into a packed restaurant inside and outside. The hostess takes us upstairs and the tables are maybe a foot apart. The restaurant itself feels like a boutique eatery tucked away in the Italian mountains. The lights are dimly lit with just enough light to see everyone you're dining with.We order our first round of drinks which is the Paloma but our lovely waitress suggest we try it with Casamigos and that's when I knew she would make sure we had a great night. For our starters we had the fried romato rice, meatballs and brussel sprouts. It's not an Italian dinner if you don't have meatballs! Each one of the starters was great in their own way but the one that stuck with me the most were the brussel sprouts. I typically order them wherever I go if I see them on the menu and not everyone cooks them well but these were perfect. A mix of soft, crunchy,seasoned and loaded with the freshest shaved Parmesan you'll ever experience. Since we all collectively decided on traditional italian appetizers, I decided to go with the squid ink campanelle for my entree. Pasta is one of my favorite dishes but I've never eaten a pasta like this before. Squid ink is typically salty but this dish was very well thought out with a delightful cream sauce, fresh crab and crunchy peppers. I've been dreaming about it since I got back to Florida and now I want to go back just for this bowl of heaven! This will be my first stop the next time I'm back in the city!
I came here for a private reception upstairs. The food was fantastic, the service was amazing, and it was really pretty. Overall great experience and I'll try the regular menu and experience soon.
Pretty disappointing. Two of us got the cacio e pepe and it was so salty that it was virtually inedible. The space was nice and the appetizers were solid, but it's hard to overcome a terrible entree.

Me, my niece, and daughter went here the 2nd night of our visit in Manhattan and I was looking forward to a good Italian meal. When our meals arrived I was taken aback as to how small my portion of $21 worth was. It was a loose tennis ball-sized portion. But the stupid thing was that it was so good! I want to go there again for that dish, but I don't want to pay that price for a dish that I can finish in 4 servings. I'll definitely learn to make it myself. My nieces dish, on the other hand, was well portioned for the price.

The dishes were well-prepared. The meatballs and squid ink campanelle were delicious, and the meal was perfectly topped off with a refreshing Amalfi lemon sorbetto. The service was average, but on a weekday afternoon, the restaurant offered a relaxed and cozy atmosphere.
Food was really yummy. Tried the linguine and broccolini and both were tasty. The hostess was weirdly sassy when she sat us, but our server was great so that made up for it

Food was very good. We got a bottle of Pinot that was fair. For appetizers we the meatballs, the Caesar salad, and the brussels sprouts. All were very good. In addition to that, for our main courses, we got chicken piccata, the ragu, the clam pasta, and the sausage/broccolini pasta. We shared them all and thought they were all good! On the hand, service was not all that. Overall not very attentive; we were never even visited after we were served our food. Then, we had to beg for our check. Kind of loud in the restaurant, but that is expected. Cute space overall. Love bar primi, overall recommend and would go again
Terrible service.  When you are paying these prices you expect the service to be more than adequate but this was horriffic.  Will not be back
Food, service, and ambience were just soo good. I got the ricotta agnolotti and it was so yummy.

Bar Primi  exceeded my expectations. The ambiance was both beautiful and inviting, creating a perfect setting for a night out. The staff were exceptionally friendly, making us feel welcome from the moment we walked in. On the second floor, Daniel, the bartender, truly stood out. His skill and personable service elevated our experience. The food was also outstanding, with each dish carefully prepared and bursting with flavor. Overall, it was a fantastic evening, and I highly recommend bar Primi for anyone looking for a memorable dining experience.

Absolutely gorgeous restaurant. One of the most beautiful I've ever been to. Lighting to die for. The food could be terrible and I'd probably still come back. However the food was so good! My husband and I shared the burrata pockets with honey and then the chicken piccata. The appetizer and the meal together were plenty for us. The waitstaff and bartenders were very nice and professional as well. We came for our anniversary dinner and I must say this is the PERFECT date night restaurant. We were both not expecting such a high quality place for the prices we saw on the menu online.

On a Sunday afternoon in July a friend and I arrived to a near by event early so we wander into Bar Primi. 

Looking for both a lite bite and a way yo past the time we perused the menu. We both decide to order grilled octopus and to share the Sicilian Caesar salad.

Both dishes were extremely tasty and service was nice. We both approved of the mountain of freshly grated Parmesan on the Sicilian Ceasar. I would stop back in for both dishes when in the area again. 

Just A Note:

The Sicilian Caesar is large enough to share. The grilled octopus is enough for an individual serving.
Not the best Italian spot in the area but serves good classics. I recommend the meatballs!

Another visit to this not fancy, not amazing, yet incredibly solid Bowery spot. Pretty easy to snag a seat.  Service attentive and down to earth.  I sat at the bar this time, as I was in a rush and alone, and got my food and drinks quickly and with a smile.

This time I had the steak frites.  I ordered medium, but received closer to rare or blue.  But flavor was good.  The "frites" was more like home fries, but crispy.  I had a couple cocktails--a frozen wine cocktail which was rich and savory, almost like a cobbler without the sweetness.  I also had the smoky Luigi--illegal mezcal, aperol, cucumber, and vermouth Bianco.  Lived up to the smoky name!

Again, this place is not mind-blowing, but it's laid back, accessible, food and drinks are decent, service is good, and close to tons of shopping, art galleries, and theater options on the Bowery.

Food was solid, service once seated was pretty hopping and friendly. Good vibe overall.
BUT 
Hostess was a drip - it's a guest's first impression of a restaurant (and lasting impression too, as they exit), and I'm not sure why you'd set someone in that role that does has a hospitable personality or demeanour. It's reason enough for me not to recommend the place,  and dock it a star if not 1.5 stars.

Some of the best Italian food I have ever had. Pasta was hearty, homemade, and perfectly cooked and the bolognese sauce was perfection. My dessert of cherry sorbet covred with a thin layer of dark chocolate was a perfect combination and eating it was delirious decadence. The whole meal was that way. And cocktails were top notch. Ambiance warm and service excellent. I could not have asked for anything more from any part of the meal. It was an extra special treat and I haven't felt that way about a restaurant in a while. Job well done to the whole restaurant team.

Went here with my friends for dinner!! 

Very responsive and easy to work with to get a reservation with!! 

We got burrata pockets and fried tomato rice (arancini) for appetizers and I got parpadelle for the entree! They were all delicious but the highlight had to be my entree; parpadelle. All the things on the menu looked very good. My friends got stuffed pasta dishes but the portion seemed so small!! 

But alas i had a great time there. They noticed we were a group of three and recommended to have three (instead of two) fried tomato rice, which was a nice suggestion. 

The inside has a bar and a little dark ambiance for the seating part, which looked cool. Outside dining was also well lit and cozy to dine at!
Cute spot for a girls night. I liked the appetizers a lot better than I liked the pasta dishes so I'd recommend coming for some drinks and apps!

My SO and I went in early October for a Saturday dinner. Both the food and service overall was disappointing. 

The food was largely forgettable and the portions minuscule for the price. We felt that we wasted our time in a city with so many other incredible options. I found it difficult to believe that Italian could be done so poorly but Bar Primi Bowery has significantly lowered my future expectations.

Service was agonizingly slow and the crowded, hot upstairs wasn't a pleasant place to sit and wait. The seating felt crammed, stuffed into a small corner table. I ended up paying in cash just to get out of there faster.

The only part I appreciated about the restaurant was the ambiance and overall decor. If you care about your time or your taste buds over the vibes of a restaurant, this is an easy place to skip.
The pastas were delicious and freshly made in house. The Caesar salad was also really good. The reservations fill up quickly so be sure to book at least a few days in advance

One of my favorite Italian restaurants in Manhattan! 

The ambiance is so warm and cozy and inviting. The servers were very attentive and helpful. The food was absolutely delicious and incredibly filling. I would totally recommend the pumpkin mezzelune! Its vegetarian, and my non-vegetarian friend said it was better than her Bolognese. Would also recommend the tiramisu, but be sure to leave room if you plan to get it, since the food is a bit heavy.

Best pasta I've ever had in my life.

The hospitality here was immaculate as well, the waiter was nothing but respectful seating us when we accidentally reserved seats for a different location.

5 stars 100% amazing place
YUMMERS! $5 miller high life was teensy tiny thoooooooo. The pasta was so gas fr. Love
Great ambiance and cozy place here for a date.night. Had a very strong espresso martini and the crostino was very unique and a filling appetizer. Bar seating is a good way to get a quick seat here.

Would honestly give this place a 8.5/10. Ambulance is truly a vibe perfect to date night or a girls night out. Food was full of flavor, and and just enough options that you don't have to be picking through so much to find out what you like. the week I came was luckily restaurant week so there was an option even though I didn't take it was still a pretty good deal. But I'm a big thing on service and the waiters were truly amazing and answered any questions I had about the menu will definitely come back.

We took my husband here for his birthday and it was a wonderful experience. The dinner was top-tier and the serving personnel very attentive. without being asked , they brought out a large sparkler at the end of meal. It was all very merry. Five stars.

This review is for the penne bolognese. It was the best dish on their menu. So many past reviews spoke very highly of this dish, so it's disappointing they got rid of it. It's been off the menu for a while now, but I haven't forgotten. RIP (bring it back)

Good place, people, service, but poor results. 

Went here on a Friday night and were sent to sit in the tight booth duo area. The setting was lovely and the servers were very attentive! 

We ordered the brussels sprouts, calamari as apps and the ravioli and parpadelle as our mains. Although the apps were the star of the show, the pasta were very lackluster. They lacked flavor and harmony with all the components. Very pricey for little.

Now I don't have a lot to compare to when it comes to NYC Italian, that being said, Bar Primi was hands down one of the best Italian restaurants I've visited. The vibe was eclectic and breathed the city. The service was swift but didn't feel rushed and the food... wow! 

We ordered a couple cocktails, a cosmo and a martini. Followed by broccoli as our appetizer... don't judge, it was fabulous. Our entrees were the pappardelle, the bucatini and a classic linguine with vodka sauce and there were no leftovers! Well done Bar Primi!

Stumbled upon this restaurant after a long walk after my visit to the Tenement Museum. I was glad it was open and pretty empty inside (I quickly learned the cold and rain does not deter New Yorkers) I was greeted and seated quickly which was great considering I was cold and already tired from my walk that morning. 

I ordered the Dante's hot toddy because I was in the mood for a warm boozy drink and this was a great choice. You could definitely taste the mulled cider with the bourbon and it helped relax and warm me up. 

I wasn't overly hungry so I chose the ricotta crostini and the insalata di scarola as a somewhat light lunch. The ricotta was extra light but creamy on the crostini and the honey was a great balance to the ricotta and nuts. Definitely a good starter. Since I love Gorgonzola, the salad was  salad was great too, just a tad overdressed with the vinaigrette dressing. Overall everything on the menu looked amazing and if I ever find myself in the area again, I'd love to come back to Bar Primi. It's located in a great area to walk in and not far from the former site of the CBGB.

Back at my favorite place in the world! 
This time here to celebrate my best friend's birthday! 
We were seated upstairs, super cute and more intimate setting for catching up. I had the johnny magazzino drink all night and my friend had non alcoholic espresso "martini" which she loved! For appetizers we had a prosciutto dish, brussel sprouts with fried pepperoni, fhe black truffle suppli (in other words like an aracini) and the ricotta with truffle honey crostini. I knew I was going to be blown away again but my friend was speechless. Thats how good. For entrees she had the sea bass dish- in her words "the best fish Ive ever had. Her husband has been here before and he has said the same. I had the linguine with garlic and breadcrumbs- it was very simple but it hit the spot. Then we shared the steak with crispy potatoes and arugula. WOW WOW WOW. I didnt think it was also going to be this good but it was the fav dish out of both of us and hands down one of my fav steal dishes ever. I dont know how they can get the potatoes cooked that way but we were obsessed!! As the finisher, they had a hazelnut special. So basically a nutella kind of situation with hazelnut ice cream and lets not forget we got the pistachio dessert! 
Cant wait to come back and highly recommend. The service was impeccable, all staff super attentive and just simply amazing. Huge shout out to Victoria for checking on us and making this dinner super special!

I was in New York visiting my brother and went to dinner here one night for very delicious Italian food! Loved the interior design and the overall vibe of the restaurant; it felt very rustic and old-school but still trendy! We were seated in a comfortable booth upstairs and the service was perfect. We ordered some drinks and then the brussel sprouts and ricotta toast as starters. Both amazing!

For my main, I ordered the pesto fusilli. I'm not typically a pasta person but this dish did not disappoint! I loved the cheese that melted into the sauce and the pasta was perfectly cooked! My boyfriend and his friend both ordered the rigatoni which they also agreed was delicious. My brother ordered the  tortellini and absolutely devoured them! 

Overall, I really had a great time dining here! Loved the food, drinks, and the atmosphere so would definitely come back! Delicious Italian food!

Bar Primi was pretty good but definitely not my favorite pasta in the city. We got the burrata pockets, bolognese, and a clam pasta that I can't quite remember the name of. I absolutely love burrata, but I found the burrata pockets to be a little underwhelming. My bolognese was good! One of the better bologneses I've had, and the clam pasta was nice as well! It had a lot of garlic flavor which I loved. We also asked for some bread to help sop up the extra sauce we had, and that was either free or they didn't charge us for it which was nice.
